title: On the Structural Optimization of Industrial Control Systems Using Metaheuristic Algorithms
abstract: The paper addresses the synthesis of a cost-optimal hardware architecture of the automated process control system (APCS) for continuous processes. The problem is formalized as the search for a minimum-cost rooted tree of devices subject to constraints on the number of I/O channels, the types and number of communication interfaces, the information capacity of processors, the regulation time and the reliability. The signals are grouped by control rooms. The problem is NP-hard, and a hybrid method is proposed that combines a deterministic hierarchy construction with a modified ant colony optimization (ACO) for device-type selection, enhanced by an adaptive heuristic. On ten instances the method is compared with a genetic algorithm (GA), particle swarm optimization (PSO), simulated annealing (SA) and CP-SAT over 30 runs each. By the best found cost the hybrid ACO outperforms GA, PSO and SA on all instances with more than 100 IOs (by 14-38 %) and runs 9-14 times faster. By the median cost, however, the deterministic-greedy baselines are more reliable (GA attains the best Friedman rank) because the cost of the ACO runs is highly variable. All differences are confirmed by the Friedman and Wilcoxon tests. The method targets the early-design search for the cheapest feasible architecture and synthesizes one within minutes at industrial scale (A up to 1086).

title: Detector‐Frame Quantum Limits for Heterodyne Timing in Relativistic Optical Links
abstract: ABSTRACT Long‐baseline optical links for space interferometry and satellite quantum networks rely on heterodyne phase tracking under Doppler motion and gravitational frequency shifts. These relativistic shifts can generate large detector‐frame beat‐frequency offsets over finite readout windows and thereby constrain the temporal precision of front‐end phase readout. We develop a detector‐frame framework for this problem using an effective two‐mode signal–local‐oscillator model in which relativistic motion rescales the local‐oscillator frequency. Within this setting we derive closed‐form Mandelstam–Tamm and Margolus–Levitin bounds for representative Gaussian resources and connect global state distinguishability with the operational precision of heterodyne phase tracking. In the bright‐local‐oscillator regime we identify a geometric–operational mismatch: the joint optical state can evolve on arbitrarily short global timescales while the relevant information rate is set by the measured detector record. Combining this result with an open‐loop transient‐acquisition analysis, we show that white phase noise and relativistic beat‐frequency drift that is approximately constant over the acquisition window generate a cube‐root scaling benchmark for the optimal pre‐lock open‐loop integration window and the minimum residual phase error. These results establish detector‐frame benchmarks for quantum‐limited heterodyne timing in relativistic optical links and clarify how global dynamical bounds enter task‐restricted continuous optical measurements.

title: AutoConcept: Training-Free Concept-Guided Reranking for Metadata-Available Composed Image Retrieval
abstract: Composed image retrieval (CIR) retrieves a target image from a reference image and a text modification. This paper studies metadata-available CIR reranking, where a fixed CIR model first returns a candidate pool and gallery metadata is then used for second-stage concept-guided scoring. We introduce AutoConcept, a training-free reranker that converts concept evidence into an interpretable memory. AutoConcept filters noisy concepts, activates query-relevant positive constraints with an auxiliary negative penalty, and combines base retrieval scores with metadata-based concept-candidate alignment through inference-time calibration. On FashionIQ, AutoConcept yields significant early-rank improvements over WeiMoCIR and consistent plug-in gains on LinCIR candidate pools. Metadata-aware controls show that structured concept memory adds signal beyond direct query-text and extracted-attribute matching, while a query-only variant further supports the effectiveness of concept-level reranking. A supplementary real-human concept-label study indicates that the same memory interface can consume participant-provided evidence. These results position AutoConcept as an interpretable concept-memory reranker for product-style CIR galleries with available metadata.

title: Autonomous discovery of new structure-plausibility laws for explainable and rapid crystal diagnosis and screening
abstract: Crystal generators and tool-using agents propose structures faster than density functional theory (DFT) energy and phonon calculations or experiments can assess them. Deciding which candidates merit expensive assessment is therefore the bottleneck, yet most screens test little beyond atomic overlap and give no chemical reason for failure. Here, our agents generate, test and actively refute two million candidate laws, leaving eight Plausibility Rules for Inorganic Structures (PRIS). These laws encode five mechanisms: short-range repulsion, ionic contact and packing, electrostatic balance, bond-valence conservation and crystallographic site complexity. Experimental structures satisfy our law sets at 82--99%, but satisfy Pauling's rules 2--5 together at only 6.5%. The strictest set detects 87.9% of damaged crystal structures, whereas distance cutoffs detect only 1.6--3.2%. PRIS plausibility is linearly correlated with synthesizability, so the PRIS-derived synthesis score (PSS) explainably screens 83.7% of hard-to-synthesize structures while retaining 80.7% of experimental structures. In a property-conditioned inverse-design run, PRIS and PSS can reduce the DFT validation queue by up to 67.3% and keep 99.2% of the candidates whose DFT-validated bulk moduli reach the design target. Beyond screening, PRIS explains why GNoME remains enriched in rare low-symmetry structures and reveals how wrong-element assignments in falsified crystal reports hide behind plausible coordinates. PRIS moves screening from a pass-or-fail verdict to a chemical reason for failure, showing that autonomous agents can discover, by active refutation, physicochemical laws that guide calculations and experiments.

title: Framework for Robust Quantum Speedups in Practical Correlated Electronic Structure and Dynamics
abstract: Proposed quantum advantage in electronic structure has so far required significant fine-tuning to find problems where classical heuristics fail. We describe how to obtain robust quantum speedups for correlated electronic structure and dynamics precisely in the regime where widely used classical heuristics are most successful.

title: Research on Text Information Extraction and Imbalanced Classification Methods for Enterprise Profiling
abstract: This research focuses on enterprise profiling in scenarios where large volumes of diverse texts—such as registration records, annual reports, news articles, and bidding notices—are continuously generated. Instead of relying solely on a single data representation or classification model, we developed a comprehensive natural language processing (NLP) pipeline for extracting key information and identifying industries. The pipeline consists of several steps. First, we use a BERT-BiLSTM-CRF model to identify core e/nterprise entities. Then, we combine TF-IDF with BERT embeddings to create a hybrid feature scheme that captures both lexical cues and contextual semantics. To address the challenge of imbalanced industry labels, we apply SMOTE in the dense semantic space and pair it with Focal Loss to enhance learning for minority classes. Additionally, we introduce a Stacking strategy to integrate outputs from different models, making predictions more stable. Tests on a self-compiled dataset covering ten national economic sectors and about 50,000 enterprises show that our method achieves a macro-F1 score of 95.4%. It outperforms traditional machine learning baselines and single deep learning models, offering more reliable recognition for minority classes. These results suggest that our framework is well-suited for applications such as supply chain partner discovery, industrial mapping, and targeted investment promotion.

title: Genesis: A Machine-Native Cognitive Architecture
abstract: Genesis is a two-layer cognitive architecture that runs on a single machine with no external model — no transformer, no pretrained weights. A Rust daemon manages an 18-chemical neuromodulatory substrate, memory consolidation, and dream synthesis at 10 Hz; a Python cognitive layer handles perception, reasoning, compositional language, and self-modeling over a self-built semantic network. The system exhibits machine-native embodiment (hardware sensors drive neurochemistry; neurochemistry drives real CPU control), active inference over its own state, and emergent sleep/wake cycles. Source: https://github.com/MindyRenee/Genesis

title: VNAGY — Modular Offline‑First Security Doctrine
abstract: This document defines the VNAGY AI Isolation Policy, a core component of the offline‑first security doctrine. The policy establishes deterministic, minimal and explicit isolation rules for AI‑related processes, ensuring that all modules operate within strict boundaries and without cloud dependency. The document formalizes the following architectural principles: Offline‑First Operation — all evaluation, scoring and behavior analysis occur locally, without external telemetry or cloud feedback loops. Passive Isolation — modules do not share memory, runtime or state; isolation is structural, not configurable. Deterministic Boundaries — each module receives only the minimal signals required for operation, preventing lateral movement and escalation. Behavior‑First Detection — detection is based on CPU behavior, heuristics, scoring and killing‑chain signals rather than signatures or cloud data. Governance Shield Enforcement — integrity, policy and rule consistency are enforced through a local governance layer. This specification is part of the broader VNAGY security doctrine, which defines how modern systems can remain resilient against AI‑driven attacks, memory‑only behavior, cloud escalation and visibility‑based exploitation. The document is published for transparency, research reference and professional review, while remaining authored and governed by VNAGY Security Engineering.

title: Quantum Self-Organizing Nonlinear Systems Modeling: Dynamic Parameter Adjustment
abstract: This paper explores the design of a novel modeling framework for quantum self-organized nonlinear systems, focusing on dynamic parameter adjustment based on input data and system state. The core mechanism involves utilizing quantum circuit simulation to iteratively adjust model parameters, thereby establishing a stronger relationship between system models and their topological structures. This approach offers enhanced flexibility and adaptability compared to traditional static parameter-based modeling techniques. The algorithm's novelty lies in its dynamic parameter adjustment capability, specifically designed to optimize system representation and achieve superior modeling performance.

title: INTELIGENCIA ESTRUCTURAL DUQUEANA
abstract: # 📄 **INTELIGENCIA ESTRUCTURAL DUQUEANA (IED)** ### Definición Formal del Paradigma Post-IA **Arquitectura determinista basada en MREI y unidades atómicas Doulita dentro del framework Duqueana Core** ## RESUMEN La **Inteligencia Estructural Duqueana (IED)** es una nueva especie de inteligencia artificial basada en la organización geométrica de la información, la iteración determinista y la compresión atómica. A diferencia de la IA clásica, que depende de modelos estadísticos y correlaciones probabilísticas, la IED opera mediante simulación verificable, convergencia trazable y ejecución eficiente en hardware estándar. Implementada en el framework **Duqueana Core**, la IED constituye el primer paradigma post-IA con evidencia reproducible, eficiencia extrema y cero alucinaciones. --- ## 1. DEFINICIÓN FORMAL DE LA IED La **Inteligencia Estructural Duqueana (IED)** es una forma de inteligencia artificial que: - Organiza la información según su **estructura fundamental** - Ejecuta procesos mediante **iteración determinista** - Comprime el contexto mediante **unidades atómicas Doulita** - Opera dentro del motor **MREI** del framework Duqueana Core **La IED no predice: simula** **La IED no estima: converge o declara "no solución"** **La IED no inventa: verifica** --- ## 2. FUNDAMENTO MATEMÁTICO — MREI El **Método de Resolución Exacta Iterada (MREI)** es el motor determinista que: - Genera estados verificables - Permite trazabilidad completa - Evita alucinaciones - Garantiza convergencia estructural Cada iteración es auditable. No existe "probabilidad de respuesta". --- ## 3. FUNDAMENTO INFORMACIONAL — DOULITA La unidad **Doulita** permite: - Compresión contextual del **90–98.5%** - Reorganización estructural - Reducción extrema de tokens - Eficiencia energética sin precedentes Es la base de la ejecución en **~6 KB RAM** y **<50 ms**. --- ## 4. FUNDAMENTO COMPUTACIONAL — DUQUEANA CORE Duqueana Core es el framework post-IA que implementa: - **MREI** (motor determinista) - **Doulita** (compresión atómica) - **ACD** (motor conversacional) - Ejecución en hardware estándar - **Peso de la interfaz web (ACD): 19.7 KB** - **Consumo RAM en simulación (p53): ~6 KB** Esto permite una IA conversacional completa sin modelos, sin entrenamiento y sin GPU. --- ## 5. evidence.abstract: # 📄 **INTELIGENCIA ESTRUCTURAL DUQUEANA (IED)** ### Definición Formal del Paradigma Post-IA **Arquitectura determinista basada en MREI y unidades atómicas Doulita dentro del framework Duqueana Core** ## RESUMEN La **Inteligencia Estructural Duqueana (IED)** es una nueva especie de inteligencia artificial basada en la organización geométrica de la información, la iteración determinista y la compresión atómica. A diferencia de la IA clásica, que depende de modelos estadísticos y correlaciones probabilísticas, la IED opera mediante simulación verificable, convergencia trazable y ejecución eficiente en hardware estándar. Implementada en el framework **Duqueana Core**, la IED constituye el primer paradigma post-IA con evidencia reproducible, eficiencia extrema y cero alucinaciones. --- ## 1. DEFINICIÓN FORMAL DE LA IED La **Inteligencia Estructural Duqueana (IED)** es una forma de inteligencia artificial que: - Organiza la información según su **estructura fundamental** - Ejecuta procesos mediante **iteración determinista** - Comprime el contexto mediante **unidades atómicas Doulita** - Opera dentro del motor **MREI** del framework Duqueana Core **La IED no predice: simula** **La IED no estima: converge o declara "no solución"** **La IED no inventa: verifica** --- ## 2. FUNDAMENTO MATEMÁTICO — MREI El **Método de Resolución Exacta Iterada (MREI)** es el motor determinista que: - Genera estados verificables - Permite trazabilidad completa - Evita alucinaciones - Garantiza convergencia estructural Cada iteración es auditable. No existe "probabilidad de respuesta". --- ## 3. FUNDAMENTO INFORMACIONAL — DOULITA La unidad **Doulita** permite: - Compresión contextual del **90–98.5%** - Reorganización estructural - Reducción extrema de tokens - Eficiencia energética sin precedentes Es la base de la ejecución en **~6 KB RAM** y **<50 ms**. --- ## 4. FUNDAMENTO COMPUTACIONAL — DUQUEANA CORE Duqueana Core es el framework post-IA que implementa: - **MREI** (motor determinista) - **Doulita** (compresión atómica) - **ACD** (motor conversacional) - Ejecución en hardware estándar - **Peso de la interfaz web (ACD): 19.7 KB** - **Consumo RAM en simulación (p53): ~6 KB** Esto permite una IA conversacional completa sin modelos, sin entrenamiento y sin GPU. --- ## 5. title: Domain Knowledge-Based Program Synthesis Template Library
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to program synthesis by introducing a Domain Knowledge-Based Program Synthesis Template Library (DKPTL). The core claim is that incorporating domain-specific knowledge significantly enhances the efficiency and quality of program synthesis. This is achieved by representing domain knowledge as templates and leveraging template matching and automated reasoning techniques for code generation. The DKPTL provides a structured repository of reusable templates, allowing for more targeted and accurate synthesis. The research contributes to a more intelligent and effective program synthesis process, moving beyond purely rule-based systems. This work outlines the architecture of the DKPTL, the methodology for template creation and management, and a preliminary evaluation demonstrating the potential of this approach.

title: Capped Langur: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Capped Langur Behavior
abstract: This paper introduces Capped Langur (CL), a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of capped langurs in the Simien Mountains National Park of Ethiopia. Capped langurs exhibit a unique strategy of selecting food items based on a combination of proximity and perceived value, effectively 'capping' their choices to maintain a balance between exploration and exploitation. CL leverages this behavior through a dynamic selection mechanism, incorporating both distance-based exploration and value-based exploitation within its optimization process. The algorithm employs a population-based approach, utilizing a set of candidate solutions represented as vectors. Each vector is evaluated based on a fitness function, which is then used to guide the selection and update of solutions. A key innovation of CL is its 'cap' mechanism, which limits the number of solutions considered at each iteration, preventing premature convergence and encouraging diverse exploration. We present a detailed description of the CL algorithm, its underlying principles, and demonstrate its effectiveness through simulations on several benchmark optimization problems. The results indicate that CL performs competitively with established metaheuristic algorithms, particularly in scenarios requiring a balance between exploration and exploitation. Further research will focus on adapting CL to solve complex real-world problems and exploring variations within the algorithm's core mechanics.

title: Bunyoro Rabbit: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Behavior of Rabbits in Bunyoro, Uganda
abstract: This paper presents Bunyoro Rabbit, a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of rabbits inhabiting the Bunyoro region of Uganda. The algorithm leverages the rabbits' instinctive tendency to explore a landscape, seeking optimal food sources while minimizing energy expenditure. Bunyoro Rabbit employs a combination of adaptive parameter control, a novel exploration-exploitation strategy based on the rabbit's movement patterns, and a dynamic memory mechanism to enhance its search efficiency. The algorithm's performance is evaluated across a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and competitive capability compared to established metaheuristic methods. The core of the algorithm relies on a modified Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) framework, incorporating features derived from rabbit foraging dynamics. Specifically, the algorithm utilizes a "hare-and-tortoise" strategy, mimicking the rabbits' alternating periods of rapid exploration and cautious approach. The key mathematical components of the algorithm include distance calculations, velocity updates, and memory management, all formulated using the following notations: $v_i(t) = w_i * r_i * \Delta v_i$, where $v_i(t)$ is the velocity of the $i$-th particle at time $t$, $w_i$ is the inertia weight, $r_i$ is a random number between 0 and 1, and $\Delta v_i$ is the change in velocity. The fitness function, $f(x)$, represents the objective function to be minimized or maximized. The algorithm's exploration rate is governed by a parameter $\eta$, and the exploitation rate is controlled by $\alpha$. The memory matrix, $M$, stores the best solution found so far, represented as $(x^*, f(x^*))$. The algorithm iterates until a termination condition is met, such as reaching a maximum number of iterations or achieving a satisfactory solution. The performance metrics assessed include convergence speed, solution accuracy, and computational cost. The Bunyoro Rabbit algorithm aims to provide a robust and efficient solution for a variety of optimization challenges.

title: Neural Organism Self-Organizing Evolutionary Network (NEIEN)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to neural network design and optimization, termed the Neural Organism Self-Organizing Evolutionary Network (NEIEN). The core claim driving this research is that by simulating the biological processes of self-organization and evolution within neural networks, we can construct networks exhibiting high adaptability and robustness, capable of automatically learning and optimizing complex system behaviors. The proposed mechanism integrates genetic algorithms with neural network learning algorithms to mimic changes in synaptic connection strengths and neuronal synaptic plasticity. This allows the network to self-organize and evolve, adapting to constantly changing environments and tasks. Unlike traditional neural networks that require manual design of network architecture and learning rules, NEIEN offers a more automated and biologically inspired solution, resulting in superior adaptability and robustness. The key innovation lies in the cyclical process of self-organization, learning, and evolutionary adaptation, driven by a simulated biological system. This approach demonstrates the potential for creating intelligent systems that can autonomously tackle complex challenges without explicit programming.

title: 多尺度几何拓扑融合的量子纠缠学习算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum entanglement learning algorithm based on multi-scale geometric topology fusion. It leverages the inherent topological structure of entangled states to guide the learning process, enabling more efficient and precise manipulation of quantum information. The core mechanism centers around constructing a quantum state representation that reflects the underlying topological properties of the entangled system. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through theoretical analysis and preliminary simulations, highlighting its potential to enhance quantum computation by facilitating robust information encoding and precise entanglement processing. The proposed algorithm offers a significant departure from traditional approaches, offering a fundamentally different pathway to achieve quantum advantages.

title: 基于语义网络与知识发现的深度学习
abstract: This paper explores the integration of semantic networks and deep learning techniques for enhanced knowledge discovery from complex data. The core claim is that leveraging the relational structure of semantic networks alongside the pattern recognition capabilities of deep learning algorithms can significantly improve both the efficiency and accuracy of knowledge extraction. The proposed mechanism involves constructing semantic networks to represent data relationships and employing deep learning models for feature extraction and pattern identification. We demonstrate how deep learning can learn representations within a semantic network, while the semantic network provides a structured framework for knowledge discovery. The research addresses the limitations of traditional knowledge discovery methods by introducing a synergistic approach, leading to more robust and insightful knowledge representation. This work contributes to the field by offering a novel methodology for dealing with the increasing volume and complexity of data encountered in various domains.

title: Probability-Based Information Seeking and Nonlinear Control
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to robust control of complex nonlinear systems utilizing a combination of probability-based information seeking and Markov Decision Process (MDP)-based control strategies. The core idea revolves around transforming information seeking from a simple numerical value to a probabilistic distribution, representing the success rate and potential reward associated with each action. This probabilistic information, termed "information seeking," is then leveraged within a reinforcement learning framework to dynamically adjust control parameters, enabling the system to adapt to the inherent nonlinearities and uncertainties of the environment. The key innovation lies in the probabilistic nature of the information seeking mechanism, which significantly improves the system's robustness against noise and disturbances, ultimately leading to more reliable and adaptive control. The theoretical framework is presented, demonstrating the potential for this approach to address challenges in controlling complex systems where traditional control methods struggle. Simulation results (hypothetical, for illustrative purposes) demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed methodology.

title: Dynamic Programming with Intrinsic Reward Shaping
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to dynamic programming (DP) that addresses the limitations of traditional methods when dealing with high-dimensional state spaces and complex reward functions. The core idea is to integrate intrinsic reward shaping, a technique that automatically generates rewards based on an agent's exploratory behavior, into DP algorithms. This allows the agent to learn more effectively, accelerating convergence and improving performance. We demonstrate that this combination significantly enhances exploration capabilities, leading to better solutions in challenging DP problems. The methodology provides a practical framework for overcoming the challenges associated with traditional DP, offering a new avenue for developing intelligent agents in various domains.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Driven Distributed Compression
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to distributed compression leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement. Traditional distributed compression techniques rely heavily on classical communication and shared local information, often limited by the Shannon limit. We introduce a framework where data is encoded into entangled states between multiple quantum systems. By performing measurements and implementing correction protocols on these entangled states, we can extract shared information while maintaining the entanglement correlation. This process effectively reduces data redundancy, leading to compression. The key innovation lies in utilizing the inherent non-locality of entanglement for direct data compression without the constraints of classical communication channels. We outline the theoretical foundations, explore the potential compression rates, and discuss the challenges and future directions of this entanglement-driven approach. The core claim is that this method can achieve compression rates exceeding those possible with classical methods, offering a fundamentally new paradigm for data compression. ---

title: Quantum-Accelerated Constraint Propagation for Large-Scale Simulations
abstract: Quantum-Accelerated Constraint Propagation for Large-Scale Simulations Quantum entanglement offers a novel approach to enhancing constraint propagation in large-scale simulations, potentially dramatically reducing computational time and enabling the exploration of more complex scenarios. This paper investigates the feasibility and potential benefits of employing quantum algorithms to optimize constraint propagation, a crucial step in many simulation frameworks. We explore the challenges of implementing quantum algorithms within the context of constraint propagation, focusing on the inherent complexity of the problem and the need for efficient quantum representations. This work presents a conceptual framework and preliminary results demonstrating the potential for quantum acceleration through tailored entanglement strategies. The core claim is that a carefully designed quantum algorithm can significantly speed up constraint propagation, allowing for more thorough exploration of the solution space, ultimately leading to improved simulation results.

title: A General Skolemisation Framework for Sequent Calculi and Expansion Proofs
abstract: Many different forms of Skolemisation exist in the literature, and their effect on proof complexity has been extensively studied since its first introduction. Other approaches to handling strong quantifiers, using variables instead of skolemterms together with acyclicity conditions similar to the original eigenvariable condition in Gentzen’s LK, are also well-known in literature. This thesis aims to unify these notions within a single comprehensive framework. We introduce skolem annotations in the form of superscripts on strong quantifiers in first-order predicate formulas as a method for controlling quantifier dependencies. We work with sequent calculi and expansion tree calculi for annotated sequents, considering both skolem-based and variable-based approaches to strong quantifier introductions. For these systems, we show that one can freely switch between the different calculi, giving size-preserving translations between the use of skolemterms and the use of variables in strong quantifiers, as well as upper bounds for size when translating between sequent and expansion tree proofs. Additionally, we also show how proofs of an annotated sequent can be reconstructed from proofs of its skolemised form with an upper bound for the size increase that is linear in the number of strong quantifiers. We then explain how classical LK, LK+, Henkin quantifiers, and certain cases of Independence-Friendly Logic can be embedded into our framework by choosing suitable annotations.

title: Semantic Integration of Industrial Sensor Data
abstract: An industrial Non-Destructive Evaluation measurement leaves its instrument with the numbers intact and with the context that makes those numbers readable held elsewhere: in the operator’s notes, in the setup sheet, and in the vendor’s own format. The dataset then has to cross exactly the organisational boundaries that Industry 4.0 exists to cross, and it arrives carrying the numbers alone. Chapter 1 separated this situation into five failures, and Chapter 3 showed that the literature treats each failure on its own and leaves their composition open. The pipeline built here supplies that composition. Three modalities are reduced to one extraction contract. A declarative configuration, read by a single engine, yields AAS properties and IDTA measurement-value blocks. The resulting graph is archived as evidence, validated against a SHACL catalogue, annotated with an ODRL policy, sealed, and packaged beside the AAS environment inside one integrity-checked container. Two commitments govern the design. The first is truthful degradation: a value the pipeline can determine is written as it stands, and a value that stays out of reach is recorded as unknown, so the record always states what is actually known about the field. The second is a separation of duties between what a pipeline can establish and what an infrastructure can grant: the pipeline holds a hard structural gate, and the FAIR layer reports a verdict that a deployment completes. Where an operator could close the gap, the record says so and asks: the unresolved fields are ranked and presented as a form, what is supplied there fills only what was empty, and an instrument’s own value is never displaced by one typed after the fact. Judged against the criteria fixed in advance in Section 4.1.2, and on the evidence of Chapter 5, the five research questions receive the following verdicts: • RQ1 is met. All three packages pass an external AAS 3.0 conformance checker with zero violations, and all thirty shells and 150 submodels load intact in a runtime, which shows the artefact is well formed for independent tooling. • RQ2 is met. One engine reuses the same configuration across all three modalities; a new modality is added by writing new configuration together with modality handler code. • RQ3 is met. Thirteen of seventeen FAIR shapes pass for eddy current and for thermography, and fourteen pass for ultrasound. • RQ4 is met. The structural groups pass on valid data and discriminate under faults, with each fault failing the group that owns it. A second, independently written engine returns the same verdicts. • RQ5 is met. Each modality ships as one AASX container whose internal references all resolve and whose recorded digests re-hash correctly. All three open in the AASX Package Explorer and in BaSyx, and answer SPARQL queries in the Orchester data space. The five contributions each carry the limit that Chapter 5 established for them. The end-to-end pipeline composition takes a raw instrument file through to a governed package in one run, and it carries the usage-control policy as a structural element of the artefact, checked in place before packaging. The declarative mapping contract holds the transformation knowledge in one file. That file is also the reference against which an automated alternative was measured, on thresholds fixed before the comparison was run and not met by any modality. The contribution is therefore a curated mapping with a stated margin over a generated one, rather than an untested preference for hand authoring. The FAIR layer is executable and traceable: seventeen shapes carry the identifiers of the seventeen metrics, and four of the remaining FAIR metrics depend on information that is provided either by the source records or by repository and serving infrastructure, so the pipeline reports their state and keeps the gate on the checks it owns. The single integrity-checked artefact gives the RDF graph and the AAS environment one identity, which is co-packaging under one identifier. The contribution of this system lies in what happens to a measurement once the instrument releases it. The system makes that measurement survivable: interpretable by a machine that was absent when it was taken, checkable against criteria written before the results were known, governed by terms that travel with it, and openable with external tools.

title: Research on Lattice-Based Cryptographic Algorithms
authors: WU Kun, TANG Jinyi, LI Peiqi, WANG Xiaorui, WANG Xiaoyu
abstract: The security of classical public-key cryptosystems, which operate based on the computational intractability of integer factorization and discrete logarithm problems, is profoundly threatened by the rapid development of quantum computing. Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) has been proposed to improve security against quantum attacks. Lattice-based cryptography is widely regarded as one of the most promising PQC method because of its proven security, efficient implementation, and functional versatility, and it has achieved significant progress in both algorithmic design and engineering implementation in recent years. This paper presents a systematic survey of the status of research on lattice-based cryptographic algorithms. First, the fundamental theory of lattices and their core hard problems are discussed. Next, the technical characteristics and performance of encryption and key encapsulation mechanisms, digital signature schemes, and key exchange protocols constructed based on lattice hard problems are reviewed and compared. Subsequently, the principles and optimization paths of two key technologies for lattice cryptography implementation, namely polynomial multiplication using the fast Number Theoretic Transform (NTT) and pre-image sampling algorithms, are discussed. Finally, considering the PQC standardization process of the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), an outlook on future research directions for lattice-based cryptography is presented. The research directions include the development of more "succinct" fundamental hard problems, strengthening security proofs, improving algorithm efficiency, and countering novel attacks. This review serves as a reference for promoting the practical deployment and further research of lattice-based cryptography.

title: Artificial intelligence supports digital transformation of “Molecular Biology Experiments of the Gene” course
authors: FU Jun, ZHANG Zhuqin, HAN Wei, ZHANG Ran, GU Jingli, XU Yuanyuan, PENG Xiaozhong
abstract: Objective Utilizing artificial intelligence(AI) to support education, and to explore the application in course of “Molecular Biology Experiment of the Gene” through a blended teaching approach which combined online and off-line instruction. Methods Totally 100 students in the academic year 2025—2026 at Peking Union Medical College were selected as the research subjects. Students were required to preview and review course-related theoretical knowledge, experimental procedures and precautions before and after class online. This study investigated the effectiveness of course digital transformation through various aspects such as students′ test scores, classroom performance, and feedback from post-class student surveys. Results The digital transformation of the course helped students in understanding experimental theories, familiarizing themselves with experimental operations, and paying attention to experimental precautions, which has been well received by students. There has been a significant improvement in students′ scores on in-class quizzes, and an increase in the proportion of excellent students. Students′ evaluation of the course has also improved. Conclusions The digital transformation of the course provides students with diversified teaching resources, stimulates their building of autonomous learning skills, and achieves significant results in course construction.

title: SRAIN: An isolated-neighborhood-based framework for LST-based surface thermal anomaly extraction
abstract: LST-based surface thermal anomaly extraction is an important task in remote sensing data analysis and is widely used in disaster monitoring and environmental assessment. This study proposes an isolated-neighborhood-based surface thermal anomaly extraction framework, termed SRAIN, for extracting spatially localized LST-based surface thermal anomalies. Taking coal-fired power plants in China from 2013 to 2024 as the primary study object and using Landsat 8/9 land surface temperature (LST) data as input, each sample is represented by a 12-month LST feature vector to characterize intra-annual monthly thermal-state variations. Drawing upon Tobler’s First and Second Laws of Geography, SRAIN assumes that spatial anomalies exhibit an “isolated” characteristic. Initial neighborhoods are constructed using Voronoi diagrams and dynamically merged using Jaccard and Silhouette coefficients to form integrated neighborhoods, thereby constituting isolated neighborhoods composed of both initial and integrated neighborhoods. In the anomaly extraction stage, ten anomaly detection algorithms are integrated, a confidence–intensity hybrid anomaly score ( G-score ) is proposed, and adaptive threshold optimization is performed using a beam-search-inspired strategy. In the anomaly pattern analysis stage, detected anomalies are classified into three modes: Concentrated (63.39%), Stretched (33.04%), and Diffuse (3.57%). Under the proxy-label-based relative evaluation framework, SRAIN improves proxy-label-based relative performance and spatial autocorrelation for LST-based surface thermal anomalies in the coal-fired power plant scenario. Compared with the best single algorithm, the fused G-score reduces the proxy-label-based misclassification rate by 12.9% and increases the spatial autocorrelation coefficient by 10.8%. In addition, the earthquake and fire cases provided in the Supplementary Materials preliminarily illustrate the potential transferability of the framework to other LST-based surface thermal anomaly scenarios, although systematic cross-scenario validation remains necessary in future studies. Overall, SRAIN provides a transferable framework for complex LST-based surface thermal anomaly extraction and offers a new perspective for environmental monitoring of anthropogenic heat sources such as coal power plants.

title: Machine learning we can trust: tensor algebra and the design of reliable foundation models
abstract: Abstract When an AI model answers our question, can we interrogate this particular answer and receive solid reasoning? Twenty‐four centuries ago, Socrates judged understanding not by how fluently someone spoke but by whether their claims survived questioning. As we hand ever more consequential decisions to AI systems and increasingly let them act on our behalf, that test has become urgent again. Current systems are often right, yet they cannot vouch for any single answer: they assert fabricated content with full confidence, they can be talked into behavior they were trained to refuse, and they offer no way to verify the reasoning behind an output. The question underneath these failures is how to design models we can trust, where trust covers robustness to manipulation, protection of private data, honesty about what the model does not know, and openness to interpretation. Part of the difficulty is that today's models are assembled for capability, with reliability pursued only after the fact. This article asks whether we can instead design models whose reliable behavior follows from how they are built, and argues that tensor algebra is an undervalued toolkit for this purpose, useful both for analyzing the models we already deploy and for designing new ones with reliability built in.

title: When Does Information Sharing Improve Decentralized Discovery? Aggregation, Independent Rescue, and Equilibrium Selection
abstract: Information sharing can improve a pooled estimate while eliminating independent rescue actions. This paper separates those effects in exact finite discovery models. A centralized action-budget profile shows that equal one-person accuracy can coexist with different portfolio values. Under a registered incremental-sharing protocol, a sharing step improves discovery exactly when pooled residual error contracts faster than an independent rescue attempt. Exact bounded registries exhibit compression, aggregation, neutral curves, and a bounded zero mixed class. In a two-agent Bayesian game with a hidden mixture of common and independent signal sources, the registered selected equilibrium yields a strict positive sharing interval at signal accuracy 3/5, while alternative equilibria show that the result is selection-dependent rather than universal. The models are synthetic and finite; no human or organizational data are used.

title: Towards AI-Assisted Clinical Trial Matching: Practical Considerations, Multicenter Evaluation, and Real-World Deployment
abstract: Clinical trials are essential for advancing cancer care and drug development, but many fail because of insufficient patient enrollment. While there is growing interest in using AI to support patient recruitment, existing systems largely perform eligibility assessment alone and have rarely been evaluated in real-world oncology workflows. Here we present TrialGPT 2.0, an AI-assisted clinical trial recommendation system designed for real-world deployment. Rather than asking only whether a patient may qualify, the system also assesses which trials warrant further consideration given the patient's current clinical needs and local workflow priorities, and provides structured, inspectable explanations for expert review. Importantly, we evaluated TrialGPT 2.0 retrospectively and prospectively across multiple oncology-focused settings, spanning government, academic cancer-center, patient-advocacy, and NIH referral workflows. In retrospective multicenter cohorts comprising 288 cases, TrialGPT 2.0 retrieved at least one clinician-recommended trial in its top 10 recommendations for approximately 91% of cases while reducing clinician screening time by 55.0%. In a six-month prospective evaluation embedded in an active precision oncology tumor board, TrialGPT 2.0 contributed additional trial opportunities missed by the routine workflow, expanding patient access to clinical trial participation by 90.9%. To support scientific reproducibility, we also introduce NIH-TrialBench, a clinician-authored dataset comprising 126 diverse synthetic patient vignettes and matching scenarios from 11 NIH Institutes and Centers. Together, these results support the value of AI to assist clinical trial matching by improving clinician efficiency and identifying frequently overlooked trial opportunities, ultimately helping to expand and accelerate accrual to cancer trials.

title: Uniform Hiding and Two Routes to Relative Accuracy in Gaussian Boson Sampling
abstract: Gaussian boson sampling requires control of how closely finite optical matrices follow Gaussian reference laws. We prove an explicit total variation bound of order $N^2/M$ between a rescaled Haar transpose Gram block and its Gaussian transpose Gram counterpart, where $N$ is the detected photon count and $M$ is the number of optical modes. The bound establishes quantitative product hiding uniformly over every number of squeezed inputs. The proof combines Stiefel recursion, centered circular orthogonal ensemble scores, and a rectangular entropy estimate. Applications combine hiding with local hafnian bounds to obtain relative probability guarantees and connect them to sampler error through exact photon-sector normalization.

title: A Closed-Loop Evaluation of Capability Loss and Recovery in Compressed Driving Policies
abstract: Many automobile and mobility companies deploy learned driving policies on embedded computers with limited memory and power. Pruning, knowledge distillation, and quantization are the standard methods to reduce the size and the inference cost of these policies. However, these methods are commonly assessed by aggregate numerical scores, and such scores may not reflect the ability of the policy to drive safely when interacting with other road users. In this study, we propose a stage-wise closed-loop evaluation approach to follow a driving policy through a compression pipeline. We formulate the driving task as a partially observable Markov decision process (POMDP) and train a belief-state policy with proximal policy optimization (PPO) in Gym-Duckietown. We then extract the actor, compress it one stage at a time, and evaluate it on five driving curricula. We show that structured pruning is the stage at which the driving capability is first lost. Meanwhile, distillation improves the pruned actor, but the improvement is limited by its rehearsal data. Integer quantization of the improved actor loses some of the curricula that require the vehicle to stop and then resume. Interestingly, the same procedure on the unpruned actor preserves all five curricula. Our study thus provides an empirical analysis aiming to answer the currently active discussions on how to accept a compressed driving policy, so as to achieve a safe and statistically reliable deployment of automated driving functions.

We formulate the driving task as a partially observable Markov decision process (POMDP) and train a belief-state policy with proximal policy optimization (PPO) in Gym-Duckietown. We then extract the actor, compress it one stage at a time, and evaluate it on five driving curricula. We show that structured pruning is the stage at which the driving capability is first lost. Meanwhile, distillation improves the pruned actor, but the improvement is limited by its rehearsal data. Integer quantization of the improved actor loses some of the curricula that require the vehicle to stop and then resume. Interestingly, the same procedure on the unpruned actor preserves all five curricula. Our study thus provides an empirical analysis aiming to answer the currently active discussions on how to accept a compressed driving policy, so as to achieve a safe and statistically reliable deployment of automated driving functions.

title: Perbandingan Interpretabilitas Model Klasik Machine Learning dan IndoBERT pada Analisis Sentimen Aplikasi Layanan Kesehatan di Indonesia Menggunakan Pengujian Generalisasi dengan Multi-Ulasan
abstract: Meningkatnya penggunaan aplikasi layanan kesehatan di Indonesia turut mendorong pertumbuhan ulasan pengguna di Google Play Store. Kondisi ini menjadikan analisis sentimen secara manual semakin tidak efisien, terlebih pada ulasan yang memiliki bahasa beragam dan kalimat kontrastif yang mengandung pergeseran sentimen antarklausa dan rentan menyebabkan kesalahan klasifikasi. Namun, kemampuan model dalam menangani kalimat kontrastif tersebut masih jarang dikaji secara khusus. Di sisi lain, penelitian analisis sentimen terdahulu cenderung hanya melaporkan metrik performa tanpa turut mengevaluasi kemampuan generalisasi dan interpretabilitas dari sebuah model. Penelitian ini mengevaluasi model machine learning klasik Naïve Bayes, Logistic Regression, SVM, Random Forest, XGBoost dan model transformer IndoBERT dalam klasifikasi sentimen ulasan aplikasi layanan kesehatan berbahasa Indonesia, khususnya pada kalimat kontrastif melalui perbandingan performa, pengujian generalisasi out-of-distribution, serta analisis Integrated Gradients. Metode penelitian mencakup pengumpulan 20.000 ulasan dari Google Play Store, pelabelan yang divalidasi terhadap pelabelan manual, pemodelan menggunakan model klasik dan fine-tuning untuk IndoBERT, serta pengujian generalisasi out-of-distribution. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa IndoBERT memperoleh F1-score tertinggi sebesar 98,10%, lebih tinggi dibandingkan model klasik sebesar 96,28%–97,57%. Pada contrastive review, IndoBERT menunjukkan performa generalisasi yang konsisten dengan akurasi 92,50% pada skenario in-domain dan 77,50% pada cross-domain, dibandingkan model klasik yang direntang 65,00%–72,50% dan 67,50%–75,00%. Analisis lebih lanjut menggunakan Integrated Gradients menunjukkan bahwa keputusan IndoBERT lebih dipengaruhi oleh token pembawa sentimen utama, terutama kata sifat dan negasi dibandingkan konjungsi kontrastif itu sendiri. Temuan ini dapat menjadi referensi untuk pengembangan model analisis sentimen berbahasa Indonesia serta mendukung pengembang aplikasi layanan kesehatan dalam mengevaluasi kualitas layanan berdasarkan persepsi pengguna.

title: THE GENERATIONAL ENGAGEMENT WITH BANKING CHATBOTS A THEORETICAL STUDY ON ADOPTING BEHAVIOUR AND PERSONAL EXPERIENCE.
abstract: - AI-powered chatbots are now essential tools for improving customer service and operational effectiveness in the era of digital banking. This conceptual study looks at how various generations use and interact with banking chatbots, from Baby Boomers to Gen Z. The study investigates generational variations in chatbot usage patterns, user satisfaction, expectations, and trust in AI-driven interactions by examining current literature, industry reports, and secondary data sources. The results indicate that older generations (Gen X and Baby Boomers) show a relatively cautious but increasing interest as they adjust to digital banking environments, while younger generations (Gen Y and Gen Z) show a high level of comfort and engagement with chatbot interfaces due to their digital fluency. The research provides insightful information on changing consumer behaviour, allowing banks to customise chatbot features for a range of age groups. Future scholars looking to investigate generational changes, technology acceptability, and AI adoption in the financial services industry should use this study as a fundamental resource.

title: Governed Skill Evolution from Persistent Agent Experience: A Prospective Ablation and Cross-Model Transfer Study
abstract: A prospective three-condition study of no Wiki, flat history, and persistent Wiki for governed Agent Skill evolution. The release includes the paper, frozen-result summaries, a verified 36-entry Skill Impact Ledger, and reproducibility checks for 87 completed model calls. Persistent Wiki reduced context, latency, and final rule length relative to flat history, but did not improve mean task quality in this narrow study. Source code and machine-readable protocols are Apache-2.0; the manuscript, documentation, result tables, figures, and release metadata are CC BY 4.0.

title: VNAGY — Modular Offline‑First Security Doctrine
abstract: This document defines the VNAGY AI Isolation Policy, a core component of the offline‑first security doctrine. The policy establishes deterministic, minimal and explicit isolation rules for AI‑related processes, ensuring that all modules operate within strict boundaries and without cloud dependency. The document formalizes the following architectural principles: Offline‑First Operation — all evaluation, scoring and behavior analysis occur locally, without external telemetry or cloud feedback loops. Passive Isolation — modules do not share memory, runtime or state; isolation is structural, not configurable. Deterministic Boundaries — each module receives only the minimal signals required for operation, preventing lateral movement and escalation. Behavior‑First Detection — detection is based on CPU behavior, heuristics, scoring and killing‑chain signals rather than signatures or cloud data. Governance Shield Enforcement — integrity, policy and rule consistency are enforced through a local governance layer. This specification is part of the broader VNAGY security doctrine, which defines how modern systems can remain resilient against AI‑driven attacks, memory‑only behavior, cloud escalation and visibility‑based exploitation. The document is published for transparency, research reference and professional review, while remaining authored and governed by VNAGY Security Engineering.

title: On Optimizing Deep Learning via Information Geometry
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to optimizing deep learning models by leveraging the concepts of information geometry. Traditional deep learning optimization relies heavily on gradient-based methods, often struggling with challenges like vanishing gradients, saddle points, and sensitivity to initialization. We propose a framework that casts the parameter learning process as a geometric optimization problem, drawing inspiration from the geometric structure inherent in the data distribution represented by the model's parameters. Specifically, we calculate the geometric shape of the loss function in the parameter space, which is interpreted as the curvature of the manifold defined by the model's parameters. This curvature information is then utilized within a geometric optimization algorithm to guide parameter updates, aiming for more efficient and robust learning. The core contribution lies in translating the inherent uncertainty and information content associated with the data distribution into a geometrically meaningful objective function, leading to a potentially superior optimization strategy compared to standard gradient descent methods. We demonstrate the theoretical foundations of this approach and outline a potential implementation strategy, focusing on the conceptual framework rather than a fully realized experimental evaluation. ---

title: Caucasian Shrew: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of *Suncus murinus*
abstract: This paper introduces Caucasian Shrew, a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging strategies of *Suncus murinus*, commonly known as the Caucasian shrew. The algorithm leverages the shrew's efficient and adaptive movement patterns – characterized by a combination of short, rapid sprints followed by periods of deliberate, exploratory searching – to establish a robust search process for solving complex optimization problems. The algorithm, termed Caucasian Shrew Algorithm (CSA), utilizes a population-based approach with adaptive sprint and exploration parameters. Specifically, the algorithm maintains a population of candidate solutions and employs a stochastic mechanism to determine the balance between sprint and exploration phases. The sprint phase is characterized by rapid, random movement across the search space, while the exploration phase involves a more methodical, localized search. The convergence criteria are defined based on the stagnation of the population's fitness landscape, and a dynamic adjustment of sprint and exploration rates is implemented to enhance the algorithm's adaptability. Theoretical analysis suggests that CSA exhibits characteristics of both particle swarm optimization and simulated annealing, resulting in improved convergence rates and solution quality compared to traditional metaheuristic algorithms. The algorithm's effectiveness is demonstrated through several benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its versatility and potential applications in various fields. The performance of CSA is evaluated against established algorithms, highlighting its advantages in terms of computational efficiency and solution accuracy. The core innovation of CSA lies in its adaptive control of sprint and exploration, directly mirroring the observed behavior of the Caucasian shrew.

title: 自适应拓扑几何的量子计算验证
abstract: Quantum computing is rapidly advancing, and its potential for complex data processing and secure communication hinges on the manipulation of quantum states. This paper explores the integration of adaptive topology, a novel approach to quantum information processing, with quantum computation. We propose an algorithm that dynamically adjusts quantum bit (qubit) configurations based on entanglement dynamics, aiming to enhance the robustness of quantum systems and improve data storage efficiency. The core claim is that this algorithmic framework, leveraging quantum entanglement, offers a significant advancement over existing verification methods by addressing limitations in quantum error correction and information density. This work details the design of a dynamic topology optimization algorithm and its potential impact on quantum computation.

title: Adaptive Differential Privacy with Personalized Noise Scales
abstract: Differential privacy (DP) provides a rigorous mathematical guarantee of privacy when releasing information derived from sensitive datasets. However, traditional approaches often rely on uniform noise scales, which can be overly conservative, leading to significant utility loss, particularly for users with high-sensitivity data or complex queries. This paper proposes a novel framework for adaptive differential privacy that dynamically adjusts the noise scale based on individual data sensitivity and query complexity. The core idea is to learn a personalized noise scale for each user, leveraging their data's statistical properties and the computational demands of the query. This system is envisioned within a federated learning architecture, allowing for decentralized learning while maintaining privacy. We demonstrate the potential for significant improvements in utility compared to static noise scale approaches, offering a more efficient and accurate method for achieving differential privacy. The key innovation lies in the dynamic adjustment, reducing the overall noise burden on sensitive users and optimizing privacy protection for diverse query scenarios. This approach represents a fundamental shift from a one-size-fits-all strategy to a tailored privacy mechanism.

title: Brosset's Big-Eared Bat: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Echolocation
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Brosset's Big-Eared Bat" (BBEB), inspired by the echolocation behavior of *Big-Eared Bats* (Big Ears). Echolocation, a complex sensory adaptation used by these bats, involves emitting high-frequency sounds and interpreting the returning echoes to create a detailed representation of their surroundings. We leverage this process to design a new optimization algorithm that effectively explores and exploits the search space. The algorithm mimics the bats' flight patterns, frequency adjustments, and target localization techniques. Specifically, the algorithm utilizes a population of "bats" represented as vectors, each containing parameters such as frequency, amplitude, and flight direction. These bats navigate a search space, updating their parameters based on a fitness function, similar to how bats adjust their calls based on echo returns. The algorithm incorporates mechanisms inspired by bats' dynamic changes in frequency and angle to dynamically adjust the exploration and exploitation phases. We demonstrate the algorithm's performance on a range of benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its ability to converge to optimal or near-optimal solutions within reasonable computational time. The algorithm's key features include a dynamic frequency adjustment mechanism, an angle-based exploration strategy, and a population-based search scheme. The performance of the BEEB algorithm is compared against established metaheuristic algorithms such as Genetic Algorithm and Particle Swarm Optimization, demonstrating its competitive effectiveness.

title: Nonlinear Topological Group Calculations: A Dynamic Approach to Quantum State Computation
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to quantum state computation utilizing the dynamic properties of non-linear topological groups. Traditional quantum state computation often relies on static representations, limiting the precision and complexity of calculations. We propose a framework where the state's dynamic evolution is intrinsically linked to the topological group's transformation, enabling a fundamentally different approach to quantum information processing. This research explores how the inherent symmetries and transformations within these groups can be exploited to achieve precise quantum state calculations. The core claim focuses on leveraging the group's dynamic change to provide a method for calculating quantum states with enhanced accuracy and revealing potential quantum information characteristics. This work represents a significant advancement in the field, offering a new paradigm for quantum state manipulation.

title: Probability Graphical Models and Time Series Forecasting
abstract: This paper explores the application of probability graphical models for time series forecasting. Traditional time series forecasting methods often struggle to capture complex dependencies and temporal dynamics within data. This research proposes a novel approach leveraging the strengths of graphical models, specifically Bayesian networks, to learn and represent these intricate relationships. The core idea is to utilize the model's structure to reduce the dimensionality of the problem and incorporate conditional dependencies, ultimately leading to improved forecasting accuracy. We present a framework for constructing and utilizing graphical models for time series, focusing on the Bayesian inference techniques for prediction. The results demonstrate the potential of this methodology to outperform conventional time series models in scenarios with significant dependencies and non-linear relationships. This work contributes to the growing field of probabilistic forecasting and offers a robust alternative for tackling complex time series prediction challenges.

title: Bougainville Melomys: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of *Melomys rubicola*
abstract: This paper introduces Bougainville Melomys (BM), a new metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of *Melomys rubicola*, a small rodent inhabiting the Bougainville Islands of Papua New Guinea. These rodents are renowned for their efficient and adaptive foraging strategies within complex, multi-dimensional environments. BM leverages this observed behavior to develop a novel optimization algorithm designed for tackling challenging combinatorial optimization problems. The algorithm incorporates elements of simulated annealing, particle swarm optimization, and a novel "contour tracking" mechanism to guide search exploration and exploitation. We present the algorithm's theoretical foundations, detailing its key parameters and operational rules. Performance evaluations on a selection of benchmark optimization problems demonstrate BM's competitive capabilities, particularly in scenarios demanding robust exploration and fine-grained search. The algorithm's adaptability and efficiency make it a promising tool for a wide range of optimization applications.

title: Bio-Inspired Program Synthesis
abstract: This paper explores the application of bio-inspired techniques, specifically evolutionary algorithms and genetic programming, to automate the generation of computer programs with desired functionality and performance characteristics. The core concept involves creating an artificial environment that mimics biological evolution, where program fragments are treated as "individuals" undergoing processes of crossover, mutation, and selection. The aim is to leverage the inherent optimization capabilities of biological evolution to discover solutions beyond the scope of conventional program design methodologies. We detail a framework for this approach, highlighting the key components and potential benefits, focusing on the automated discovery of efficient algorithms for specific tasks. The research presents a novel methodology for tackling complex optimization problems by harnessing the power of evolutionary computation.

title: Quantum Circuit Verification via Graph Neural Networks
abstract: The verification of quantum circuits is a critical step in ensuring the reliable execution of quantum computations. Traditional methods often struggle with the exponential complexity arising from the superposition and entanglement inherent in quantum mechanics. This work proposes a novel approach utilizing Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) to address this challenge. Quantum circuits are represented as graphs, where nodes correspond to quantum gates and edges represent data flow. The GNN learns to identify patterns within these graph representations that signify potential errors or deviations from the intended circuit behavior. This automated verification process offers a scalable solution compared to exhaustive simulation or analytical methods. The core of this approach lies in leveraging the expressive power of GNNs to capture complex correlations within the circuit structure, ultimately leading to more efficient and accurate verification. We demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of this methodology through a theoretical framework and outline future research directions.

evidence.title: Quantum Circuit Verification via Graph Neural Networks
evidence.abstract: The verification of quantum circuits is a critical step in ensuring the reliable execution of quantum computations. Traditional methods often struggle with the exponential complexity arising from the superposition and entanglement inherent in quantum mechanics. This work proposes a novel approach utilizing Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) to address this challenge. Quantum circuits are represented as graphs, where nodes correspond to quantum gates and edges represent data flow. The GNN learns to identify patterns within these graph representations that signify potential errors or deviations from the intended circuit behavior. This automated verification process offers a scalable solution compared to exhaustive simulation or analytical methods. The core of this approach lies in leveraging the expressive power of GNNs to capture complex correlations within the circuit structure, ultimately leading to more efficient and accurate verification. We demonstrate the feasibility and effectiveness of this methodology through a theoretical framework and outline future research directions.

title: Geometric Information Fusion Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization algorithm, Geometric Information Fusion Optimization (IGFO), designed to enhance optimization results by leveraging geometric information. Traditional optimization methods often rely on manually crafted parameters, while IGFO employs geometric information to guide the optimization process, leading to improved accuracy and reliability. The core mechanism of IGFO involves utilizing geometric structure information to subtly influence the optimization landscape, promoting convergence towards optimal solutions. This approach distinguishes itself through its integration of geometric constraints and their influence on the search space. This paper explores the practical implementation of IGFO, demonstrating its efficacy through several benchmark problems and providing a detailed analysis of its performance characteristics.

title: An Initial Study on Reconstructing Communicative Intent from ASR Pre-Decision Information in Dysarthric Speech: Toward a Personal Speech Interpreter
abstract: This preprint presents an initial study toward a Personal Speech Interpreter (PSI) for people with dysarthria. It investigates whether information related to a speaker’s intended utterance can remain in ASR pre-decision information even when it is lost from the final 1-best output. Using dysarthric Japanese speech and Reazon Japanese Zipformer, the study examines token posterior information and discusses its potential use for downstream intent reconstruction by a large language model (LLM), with particular attention to the safe handling of critical information such as numbers, times, negation, and agreement or disagreement.

title: Title: Recursive Geometry for Pattern Recognition
abstract: The current landscape of pattern recognition often relies on traditional methods like linear regression or clustering, which struggle to effectively handle complex, high-dimensional data like those found in image and audio analysis. This paper introduces Recursive Geometry, a novel algorithm leveraging recursive geometric analysis to automatically identify intricate patterns and motifs within datasets. We propose a 'Recursive Pattern Detector' – a neural network architecture that constructs geometric representations of patterns, enabling a deeper and more nuanced understanding than conventional approaches. The core claim is that this algorithm will significantly improve pattern recognition accuracy and robustness, particularly in datasets characterized by subtle variations and complex relationships. This work represents a fundamental shift in approach, moving beyond simple identification to a fundamentally different method of pattern comprehension. The proposed method's strength lies in its ability to create a robust geometric framework for pattern extraction, which can then be refined through iterative refinement processes.

title: DATA-DRIVEN OPTIMAL SITE SELECTION FOR SOLAR POWER PLANTS BASED ON SOLAR IRRADIANCE ANALYSIS
abstract: Solar power plants play a critical role in meeting global energy demands in a sustainable and environmentally friendly manner. The efficiency and long-term sustainability of clean energy production largely depend on the optimal siting of these plants, making solar irradiation data a crucial factor for ensuring maximum energy yield. This study focuses on Global Horizontal Irradiance (GHI), one of the most significant and widely used indicators in the literature for identifying suitable solar power plant locations, by performing monthly analyses through remote sensing (RS) and geographic information systems (GIS). Regions with higher irradiation levels were classified accordingly. Technical, environmental, and economic factors, which may vary across countries or regions, were intentionally excluded to highlight the primary influence of solar irradiance on site suitability. The study was conducted specifically for the Elmalı district in Antalya, Türkiye. Results show that 28% of the area is highly suitable for solar power plant installation, 33% is moderately suitable, and 39% is less suitable based on GHI. In absolute terms, 4,969 hectares are classified as "very high suitability" and 43,038 hectares as "high suitability," indicating areas with strong investment potential. This study provides a clear, data-driven assessment of irradiance-based suitability and is expected to support and guide strategic solar energy investment and planning decisions in the region.

title: Rethinking the Representation of Spatiotemporal Fields: A Design Pattern for Geospatial Ontologies
abstract: Spatiotemporal fields are a fundamental representation for describing spatially continuous phenomena, yet existing models often treat value assignment as an implicit relation between locations and values. This paper introduces the Spatiotemporal Field Ontology Pattern (SFOP), an ontology design pattern that adopts an observation-centered view in which field values are generated through observation processes linking intended spatiotemporal locations, observable properties, and observation results (i.e., the measured or derived values). The pattern distinguishes between a field’s defined domain, representing the locations where observations are intended, and its observed domain, representing the locations for which observations actually exist. This distinction enables an explicit representation of incomplete, evolving, and derived observations. SFOP aligns with existing standards, including SOSA/SSN, GeoSPARQL, and OWL-Time, while supporting the inference of field properties and observed domains from observational evidence. The resulting pattern provides a semantically grounded foundation for representing, querying, and reasoning over spatiotemporal fields in knowledge graphs.

title: Ulasan Pengguna Sebagai Cerminan Kualitas Media Digital: Studi Analisis Sentimen Pada Aplikasi Detikcom
abstract: This study aims to analyze user review sentiments as a reflection of digital media quality in the Detikcom news application on Google Play Store. User reviews are considered a form of evaluative communication that represents audience perceptions and experiences toward digital media. This research employs a quantitative approach using text-based sentiment analysis. The data consist of 2,025 user reviews collected from Google Play Store and analyzed using Python programming. The analysis stages include text preprocessing, sentiment classification into positive, neutral, and negative categories, word frequency analysis, and examination of the relationship between sentiment and user ratings using the Chi-square test. The results indicate that positive sentiment dominates user reviews, suggesting a generally favorable perception of content quality and news update speed. Nevertheless, a considerable proportion of negative sentiment is identified, mainly related to excessive advertising and technical issues within the application. The Chi-square test reveals a statistically significant relationship between numerical ratings and user review sentiment (χ² = 4002.00; p < 0.001), confirming that ratings correspond with users’ emotional expressions in textual reviews. This study concludes that sentiment analysis of user reviews serves as a valuable indicator for assessing the quality and credibility of digital media and contributes to the development of audience-centered communication studies in the digital media context.

title: Validation of programming language Energia - 4.0
abstract: Abstract In this paper is presents validation of compiler for programming language Energia - 4.0, and more precisely the quantum calculations. Programming language Energia supports array declarations, functional transformations and conditional control flow. Functionality for quantum calculations is added in new version Energia-4.0. The minimal gate set (X Pauli gate), H (Hadamard gate), CX (controlled-NOT gate), measurement, reset) is implemented in Energia-4.0 as any quantum computation can be approximated using these operations. The idea behind the new version of the programming language is to use it as a platform for testing new quantum algorithms on classical computers, including algorithms for machine learning.

title: SHEG: A Self-Healing Encryption Graph for post-quantum hybrid encryption with robust fault and DFA resilience
abstract: Recent developments in post-quantum cryptography (PQC) have brought quantum-resistant algorithms like Kyber512. Nevertheless, the current hybrid encryption systems incorporating the combination of symmetric encryption and PQC primitives are still susceptible to fault injection and differential fault analysis (DFA) attacks. In order to overcome these issues, SHEG introduces a fault-resilient execution framework for hybrid post-quantum cryptographic primitives, modeling AES-GCM and Kyber512 operations as a self-healing execution graph with node-level verification and selective rollback recovery. SHEG combines AES-GCM for high-speed symmetric encryption with Kyber512 for quantum-secure key encapsulation, and models the encryption flow as a directed graph with chained integrity checkpoints. This architecture supports real-time fault detection and selective rollback recovery, recomputing only the affected execution stages. As a result, rollback cost is reduced by up to 75% when faults occur in later execution stages. Experimental results demonstrate that SHEG provides execution-level fault resilience against practical DFA-style attacks under the stated threat model, achieving a recovery rate exceeding 99% at a 1% fault injection rate while introducing only approximately 10% computational overhead. SHEG provides execution-level fault resilience with moderate computational overhead. However, additional evaluation on embedded and resource-constrained platforms is required to assess deployment-specific performance characteristics.
