title: Training Without Gathering the Data: A Historical Development Review of Federated Learning and Privacy-Preserving AI
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Federated Learning and Privacy-Preserving AI in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of federated learning and privacy as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: The Use of Artificial Intelligence in the Process of Marketing Management in Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises
abstract: Purpose: The primary objective of this study was to determine how the use of artificial intelligence tools affects the efficiency of marketing management in small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Poland, based on original research.To achieve this objective, the study identified the marketing areas where artificial intelligence (AI) is most frequently employed, assessed entrepreneurs' awareness and knowledge regarding AI, analyzed the benefits, barriers, and limitations associated with its implementation, evaluated the impact of AI usage on operational efficiency, and outlined prospects for future development.Design/Methodology/Approach: This study employs a survey-based research method using a questionnaire.The questionnaire was designed to gather information on the extent to which enterprises use artificial intelligence tools in their marketing activities, the assessment of their effectiveness, the marketing areas supported by AI technologies, and the barriers and challenges associated with implementing these solutions in practice.Findings: The results clearly indicate that AI is no longer merely an experimental technology but has become one of the most common optimization tools.High levels of awareness and implementation of AI tools within enterprises were also observed.SME managers view AI as a key element in building a competitive advantage, enabling them to bridge the resource gap vis-à-vis large corporations.The dominant model of AI adoption is task automation.The popularity of using AI for content creation, managing marketing campaigns, and data analysis suggests that the technology is viewed primarily as a tool for automating tasks.The main benefit for organizations is not a direct reduction in financial costs-in this regard, the gains for the enterprise are usually negligible or minor.However, the radical optimization of working time is the primary driver behind the popularity of AI tools.Current trends in how these tools are implemented within enterprises suggest that the approach to human resource utilization may undergo a significant shift in the coming years, with a growing trend of moving personnel away from routine tasks toward conceptual or strategic activities.Practical Implications: Leveraging AI in marketing management within SMEs significantly boosts effectiveness and improves overall business performance.However, success in this area will increasingly depend not merely on the technology itself, but on the organization's ability to adapt and educate itself in order to avoid falling behind in the digital landscape.

title: Machine learning-enhanced modified early warning system for predicting in-hospital mortality on pulmonary ward
abstract: Background: Early recognition of impending systemic failure and timely delivery of appropriate medical care are critical for effective clinical intervention. The Modified Early Warning Score (MEWS) is widely used to identify patients at risk of clinical deterioration. However, as patient complexity increases—driven by advanced age, multimorbidity, and other risk factors—automated warning systems often generate excessive alerts, leading to high false-alarm rates. Therefore, we aim to develop and validate a machine learning-enhanced predictive model (MEWS+) to detect critical in-hospital mortality risk factors earlier, thereby supporting clinical decision-making and optimizing acute care triage on pulmonary wards. Methods: This retrospective cohort study analyzed electronic health records from 4,108 consecutive adult patients admitted to the pulmonary wards of a medical center between January and June 2021. Four machine learning (ML) frameworks—extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), random forest, logistic regression, and support vector machine—were trained and evaluated using an 80:20 data split. Pairwise nonparametric Spearman rank correlation was used to assess associations between baseline predictors and in-hospital mortality. Results: Among the 4,108 patients included, the cohort was predominantly elderly (60.6% aged ≥65 years) and female (61.6%), with males accounting for 38.4%. The baseline in-hospital mortality rate was 5.4%, representing 222 empirical mortality events. Spearman correlation analysis showed that the recalculated traditional MEWS score had the strongest positive monotonic association with in-hospital mortality (ρs =0.430, P<0.05), followed by signed do-not-resuscitate (DNR) status (ρs =0.383, P<0.05), MEWS time (ρs =0.292, P<0.05), and age (ρs =0.204, P<0.05). In contrast, chronic comorbidities demonstrated very weak correlations (heart failure: ρs =0.079; hypertension: ρs =0.035). On the independent testing set, the XGBoost classifier achieved the highest predictive performance, with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.970 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.944–0.990], sensitivity of 0.872 (95% CI: 0.743–0.952), and specificity of 0.972 (95% CI: 0.957–0.982). Feature-importance analysis indicated that the MEWS score (0.402), signed DNR status (0.194), and MEWS time (0.136) were the primary contributors to model performance. Conclusions: An ML-enhanced MEWS+ model by effectively balancing clinical sensitivity and operational precision, by integrating acute physiological indicators with advanced directives and demographic factors, the XGBoost-based MEWS+ system provides highly accurate, individualized early-warning triage to strengthen clinical safety on general hospital wards.

title: Thought-Mediated Learning: From Deliberative Reasoning to Automatic Behavior
abstract: Autonomous agents require not only deliberate reasoning for unfamiliar situations but also the ability to convert repeatedly useful reasoning into efficient automatic behavior. However, existing LLM-based agents and knowledge-distillation approaches generally couple reasoning and learning through predefined training objectives or direct teacher--student supervision, leaving unclear how an agent can autonomously determine what should become learned behavior. This paper proposes Thought-Mediated Learning (TML), a framework that separates LLM-based deliberative thinking from an independent ML/DL background learning process. Thinking cannot directly update the automatic model; instead, it produces thought materials whose content and frequency determine what becomes available for learning. Repeated thinking implicitly strengthens important experiences, attention determines which factors are represented, jointly considered events may create spurious associations, and imagined experiences can provide learning materials before corresponding real events occur. Observed outcomes further generate corrective materials that revise previously learned automatic behavior. Experimental results show that TML achieves 96.67% hidden-pattern acquisition and 99.93% post-learning automatic accuracy, reaches 97.83% OOD (out-of-distribution) accuracy versus 9.50% for raw learning, and improves zero-real rare-case success to 59.38% while corrective learning raises final hidden-case success to 96.82%.

Repeated thinking implicitly strengthens important experiences, attention determines which factors are represented, jointly considered events may create spurious associations, and imagined experiences can provide learning materials before corresponding real events occur. Observed outcomes further generate corrective materials that revise previously learned automatic behavior. Experimental results show that TML achieves 96.67% hidden-pattern acquisition and 99.93% post-learning automatic accuracy, reaches 97.83% OOD (out-of-distribution) accuracy versus 9.50% for raw learning, and improves zero-real rare-case success to 59.38% while corrective learning raises final hidden-case success to 96.82%.

title: Συστηματική υποβοήθηση νεοφυών επιχειρήσεων με χρήση τεχνικών τεχνητής νοημοσύνης
abstract: Η παρούσα διδακτορική διατριβή εξετάζει το πρόβλημα της συστηματικής υποβοήθησης και αξιολόγησης νεοφυών επιχειρήσεων (startups) με τη χρήση τεχνικών Τεχνητής Νοημοσύνης. Οι νεοφυείς επιχειρήσεις πρώιμου σταδίου (early stage startups) λειτουργούν υπό συνθήκες αυξημένης αβεβαιότητας, περιορισμένων οικονομικών και ανθρώπινων πόρων και άνισης πρόσβασης σε εξειδικευμένη καθοδήγηση. Οι παραδοσιακοί μηχανισμοί υποστήριξης, όπως οι σύμβουλοι, οι θερμοκοιτίδες και οι επιταχυντές, παρέχουν σημαντική εμπειρογνωμοσύνη, αλλά περιορίζονται ως προς το κόστος, τη διαθεσιμότητα και τη δυνατότητα κλιμάκωσης. Παράλληλα όμως, η διάδοση της Παραγωγικής Τεχνητής Νοημοσύνης και των Μεγάλων Γλωσσικών Μοντέλων (LLMs) δημιουργεί αναντίλεκτα νέες δυνατότητες για παροχή καθοδήγησης κατά απαίτηση, χωρίς όμως να επιλύει αυτομάτως το πρόβλημα. Η χρήση μοντέλων γενικού σκοπού (LLMs) σε ρόλο συμβούλου ή αυτόνομου αξιολογητή συνοδεύεται, λόγω του τρόπου λειτουργίας τους, από παραισθήσεις (hallucinations), εξάρτηση από στατικά δεδομένα, τάση συγκατάβασης προς τις υποθέσεις του χρήστη (sycophancy), αστάθεια της βαθμολόγησης και περιορισμένη προσαρμογή τόσο στο στάδιο ανάπτυξης όσο και στο επιχειρηματικό πλαίσιο κάθε startup. Σκοπός της διατριβής είναι ο σχεδιασμός, η υλοποίηση και η εμπειρική αξιολόγηση ενός ολοκληρωμένου υπολογιστικού τεχνουργήματος, του Evaluator.GR, το οποίο υποστηρίζει συστηματικά τη διαδρομή μιας νεοφυούς επιχείρησης από τη διαμόρφωση και την επικύρωση της αρχικής ιδέας έως την προετοιμασία για χρηματοδότηση και την επενδυτική ετοιμότητα. Η έρευνα δεν αντιμετωπίζει την Τεχνητή Νοημοσύνη ως συνολικό υποκατάστατο του ανθρώπινου μέντορα, αξιολογητή ή επενδυτή, αλλά ως υποδομή υποστήριξης της ανθρώπινης κρίσης και αυτοματοποίησης επιμέρους εργασιών, με έμφαση στην αξιοπιστία, στην τεκμηρίωση, στην επεξηγησιμότητα και στην υπεύθυνη χρήση. Ως κύριο μεθοδολογικό πλαίσιο υιοθετήθηκε η Έρευνα Επιστήμης Σχεδιασμού (Design Science Research), μέσω των αλληλοτροφοδοτούμενων Κύκλων Συνάφειας, Σχεδιασμού και Αυστηρότητας. Στον Κύκλο Συνάφειας πραγματοποιήθηκε Συστηματική Ταχεία Αξιολόγηση Τεκμηρίων, η οποία χαρτογράφησε τις εφαρμογές, τις συνθήκες απόδοσης και τους περιορισμούς της Παραγωγικής Τεχνητής Νοημοσύνης (generative AI) στην καθοδήγηση και αξιολόγηση startups. Τα αναγνωρισμένα ερευνητικά κενά μετασχηματίστηκαν, στον Κύκλο Σχεδιασμού, σε λειτουργικές και αρχιτεκτονικές απαιτήσεις του Evaluator.GR. Στον Κύκλο Αυστηρότητας, το τεχνούργημα αξιολογήθηκε μέσω συγκριτικής μελέτης έναντι μοντέλων γενικού σκοπού και μέσω πιλοτικής εφαρμογής σε πραγματικές νεοφυείς επιχειρήσεις.Το υπολογιστικό τεχνούργημα (artifact) που αναπτύχθηκε είναι το Evaluator.GR, μια πολυαρθρωτή πλατφόρμα αξιολόγησης, στρατηγικής υποστήριξης και παραγωγής επιχειρηματικών παραδοτέων. Η αρχιτεκτονική του συνδυάζει Μίξη Ειδικών σε επίπεδο συστήματος (System-Level Mixture of Experts), τριπλό αξιολογητή και επιπροσθέτως μηχανισμό Μετα-Αξιολογητή (Meta-Judge). Παράλληλα όμως, χρησιμοποιεί σταδιο-προσαρμοστικές ρουμπρίκες (rubrics), παραγωγή με ενίσχυση ανάκτησης (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) και αναζήτηση στον Παγκόσμιο Ιστό (world wide web). Η ανθρώπινη εποπτεία ενσωματώνεται λοιπόν σε τρία (3) επίπεδα. Οι μηχανισμοί αυτοί σχεδιάστηκαν ώστε να περιορίζουν την εξάρτηση από έναν μεμονωμένο LLM γενικού σκοπού, να ενισχύουν τη γείωση και την τεκμηρίωση των αποτελεσμάτων και να διατηρούν την τελική ευθύνη στον άνθρωπο. Παράλληλα, η πλατφόρμα αναπτύχθηκε με αρχές Συμμόρφωσης βάσει Σχεδιασμού, σε ευθυγράμμιση με το EU AI Act και το NIST AI Risk Management Framework. Τα δεδομένα αξιολόγησης προήλθαν από τρεις συμπληρωματικές πηγές. Η Συστηματική Ταχεία Αξιολόγηση Τεκμηρίων περιέλαβε τριάντα τέσσερα (34) τελικά τεκμήρια της περιόδου 2022–2025. Η συγκριτική μελέτη πραγματοποιήθηκε με 139 αξιολογητές, 52 στην ελληνόφωνη και 87 στην αγγλόφωνη ομάδα, οι οποίοι αξιολόγησαν το Evaluator.GR, το Gemini 3 και το ChatGPT 5.2 σε δεκατέσσερις (14) διαστάσεις. Επιπλέον, υλοποιήθηκε πιλοτική εφαρμογή διάρκειας 30 ημερών με 10 νεοφυείς επιχειρήσεις στα στάδια Pre-seed και Seed. Στη συγκριτική αξιολόγηση, το Evaluator.GR έλαβε συνολικό μέσο όρο 4,51/5, έναντι 3,64/5 για το Gemini 3 και 2,37/5 για το ChatGPT 5.2. Τα ποιοτικά ευρήματα του πιλοτικού προγράμματος έδειξαν ότι το σύστημα μπορούσε να εντοπίζει ουσιώδεις επιχειρηματικές ή τεχνικές αδυναμίες και να παρέχει προσαρμοσμένες συστάσεις, ανέδειξαν όμως και περιπτώσεις στις οποίες απαιτήθηκαν ανθρώπινη παρέμβαση, επανεξέταση ή βαθμονόμηση των αποτελεσμάτων. Η συνεισφορά της διατριβής είναι θεωρητική, μεθοδολογική, τεχνική και πρακτική. Συνδέει τη βιβλιογραφία για την υποστήριξη startups με GenAI, το LLM-as-a-judge και την Υπεύθυνη Τεχνητή Νοημοσύνη (Responsible AI) με το πλαίσιο Mentor–Evaluator Stack, ενσωματώνει τη βιβλιογραφική σύνθεση, την κατασκευή και την εμπειρική αξιολόγηση στο πλαίσιο της DSR και προτείνει μια πολυπρακτορική, σταδιο-προσαρμοστική και ελεγχόμενη αρχιτεκτονική υποστήριξης της ανθρώπινης κρίσης. Τα αποτελέσματα, ωστόσο, αφορούν την αντιλαμβανόμενη ποιότητα, χρησιμότητα και αξιοπιστία στο συγκεκριμένο πλαίσιο αξιολόγησης. Δεν τεκμηριώνουν αιτιώδη επίδραση στη χρηματοδότηση, στην επιβίωση ή στη μακροχρόνια ανάπτυξη των startups. Πρόσθετοι περιορισμοί είναι η μικρή διάρκεια και κλίμακα του πιλοτικού προγράμματος, η εξάρτηση από συγκεκριμένες εκδόσεις μοντέλων, ρουμπρίκες και διαθέσιμα δεδομένα, καθώς και η λειτουργική επιβάρυνση που εισάγουν οι μηχανισμοί ανθρώπινης εποπτείας.

title: Enhancing retrieval-augmented generation via domain-adaptive embedding optimization: a unified fine-tuning strategy
abstract: With the growing adoption of Large Language Models (LLMs) in diverse fields, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has emerged as a pivotal paradigm to mitigate hallucinations and knowledge obsolescence. However, generic embedding models often falter when applied to vertical domains, suffering from a domain gap that compromises retrieval accuracy. This paper proposes a domain-adaptive embedding optimization scheme based on a Unified Fine-Tuning strategy. Furthermore, addressing the challenge of data scarcity in specialized fields, we introduce a novel dataset construction pipeline utilizing LLMs for data augmentation and hard negative mining. By leveraging this high-quality contrastive data and specialized loss functions, our approach synergistically optimizes retrieval recall and ranking precision within a single-stage bi-encoder architecture. Empirical results on vertical domain datasets demonstrate that our solution significantly outperforms baselines, particularly in the medical domain, improving MRR@10 and NDCG@10 by 3.4% and 2.7%, respectively. This study provides a concise, cost-effective, and architecturally efficient path for adapting RAG systems to specialized industrial contexts.

title: What is a Conditional?
abstract: Abstract This paper examines the nature of conditionals in thought, natural language, and logic. It argues that conditionals are fundamentally concerned with possibilities rather than merely with truth values, and distinguishes several types of conditional according to the relation between antecedent and consequent. Particular attention is given to implicative and concessive conditionals. An implicative conditional is characterized as one in which the antecedent is taken to imply the consequent, whereas in a concessive conditional the consequent holds despite the antecedent providing a reason for its falsity. A modal definition of the implicative conditional is proposed according to which the conjunction of the antecedent with the negation of the consequent is impossible, while the contingency of both antecedent and consequent is treated as a presupposition. This account is compared with material implication, C. I. Lewis’s strict implication, and Pizzi’s consequential implication. A logical definition is also proposed for the concessive conditional according to which the antecedent is contingent, the consequent necessary, and a new operator symbolizes the antecedent as a reason for the falsity of the consequent. The paper also examines the negation of conditionals and squares of opposition generated by relations among implicative and concessive conditionals and their negation. Finally, it briefly discusses three further types of non-implicative natural-language conditionals and argues that logical systems should be assessed partly by how adequately their conditional operators capture the relations of implication and consequence found in natural reasoning.

The paper also examines the negation of conditionals and squares of opposition generated by relations among implicative and concessive conditionals and their negation. Finally, it briefly discusses three further types of non-implicative natural-language conditionals and argues that logical systems should be assessed partly by how adequately their conditional operators capture the relations of implication and consequence found in natural reasoning.

title: Beyond "AI Helps Humans": Decision-Targeted Evaluation Design for Human-Agent Teams in the Agentic Era
abstract: Wherever a coding agent works under engineer supervision, or a clinical model assists a radiologist, the deployment question is whether to keep the human-AI workflow or replace it with the human alone or the agent alone. The human-AI workflow is worth keeping only if it beats both of those alternatives. Yet once it is deployed, neither alternative outcome is observed: recovering one means replaying the task under that alternative, and every replay costs expert time or compute. Under a fixed replay budget, the design question is therefore which tasks should be more likely to receive a human-only replay, and which an agent-only replay. Existing methods do not directly target this decision. Agent benchmarks do not choose which missing baseline to measure, variance-based sampling ignores which of the two comparisons is closer to failing, and Bayesian information methods focus on learning model parameters instead of making the deployment decision. We propose TEAM-Design, a rule that gives every task two replay probabilities, one per baseline. It raises a probability where the missing baseline outcome is hard to predict from what is already known about the task and where that comparison is harder to establish, and lowers it where replay is expensive. We prove that the rule solves this budgeted design problem, and that drawing the replays at random from recorded probabilities still controls the chance of wrongly declaring that the workflow beats both. We reanalyze 6 clinical settings, where no human-AI workflow beats both alternatives, and a coding benchmark, where one does, then evaluate TEAM-Design on synthetic designs and on a semi-synthetic design built from a real chest X-ray reader study. TEAM-Design works best when one of the two comparisons is clearly harder to settle than the other, and can do worse than variance-based allocation when the two are similarly difficult.

title: Citing Less Critically: LLMs Reshape the Rhetoric and Reach of Scientific Citation
abstract: Scientific citations carry rhetorical intent. Scholars may cite prior work positively (supporting), negatively (contrasting), or neutrally (mentioning). As large language models (LLMs) increasingly assist scientific writing, whether they reproduce citations with the same rhetorical intent as humans remains unclear. We introduce a masked-citation task to compare human and LLM-generated citation behavior. For each citation context, an LLM generates a replacement citation sentence, producing a counterfactual corpus directly comparable to human citation. We analyze what, whom, and how models cite, using an LLM-as-a-judge to classify citation intent and a 20-million-edge coauthorship network to measure social distance between cited authors. Across six popular LLMs and 1,746 top NLP conference papers (63k+ contexts, 132k+ citations), three patterns emerge: (1) Compared with human citation, LLMs cite significantly less critically; (2) LLMs over-cite popular and older papers, a tendency amplified for contrasting citations where human writing more often draws on recent, niche work; (3) Whereas humans often cite within their close social network, especially for supporting citations, LLMs tend to draw on more socially distant authors. Together, these differences are double-edged: LLM citation reaches beyond a scholar's close collaborators while being less critical and amplifying visibility bias, reshaping the rhetoric and reach of scientific citation.

title: Athena: Vulnerability-Affected Library Identification via Knowledge Graph Completion
abstract: A single vulnerability in a widely used library can cascade through millions of dependent applications, yet more than half of vulnerability database entries contain missing or incorrect affected-library information. Existing automated approaches neglect the relational structure of vulnerability databases, treating identification as an isolated text retrieval problem. In this paper, we propose Athena, the first graph-based approach for vulnerability affected library identification. Athena models vulnerability databases as a knowledge graph and reformulates the identification problem as knowledge graph completion (KGC). It comprises three key modules: a Modeling module that constructs a security knowledge graph integrating CVEs, libraries, CWE weakness types, CPE products, and software ecosystems; a Completion module that applies a modular KGC backbone to predict missing affected libraries for a given CVE via link prediction; and a Re-ranking module that retrieves KGC candidates and rescores them using a fine-tuned LLM augmented with knowledge graph embeddings, jointly leveraging structural and textual information. Our experiments on VulLib demonstrate that Athena significantly outperforms four state-of-the-art baselines, achieving a 32% improvement in Avg. F1 over the best baseline (i.e., VulLibGen). Notably, our KGC backbone with only 110M parameters already surpasses VulLibGen's best configuration at 7B parameters, demonstrating the effectiveness of graph-based modeling; the re-ranking module then provides substantial further gains, consistently outperforming the best baseline across all evaluated LLM backbones.

title: VIBE-Bench: Evaluating Personalized Large Language Models When Profiles Don't Mean Preferences
abstract: Personalized Large Language Models (PLLMs) aim to tailor responses to individual users, where a central challenge is preference reasoning: inferring query-relevant preferences from user-related history. Existing benchmarks, however, largely assume that such preference can be retrieved from semantically related history. We study an underexplored but practically important regime, profile-preference conceptual misalignment (PRCM), where observable profile cues and query-specific preferences lie in different concept spaces, making semantic retrieval inconsistent for personalization. We introduce VIBE-Bench, a benchmark with two psychology-grounded tasks, 3,504 personas and 12,239 dialogues, including a manually verified gold test set, and requires cross-concept preference reasoning beyond surface semantic overlap. Experiments with several personalization methods show that current PLLMs largely rely on shallow semantic correlations and fail to acquire robust cross-concept mappings. These findings establish PRCM as a distinct failure regime in PLLMs and position VIBE-Bench as a focused testbed for advancing preference reasoning beyond semantic matching.

title: EarthLD: Towards Unified Open-World Landslide Understanding via Vision-Language Guided Diffusion Models
abstract: Landslides are widespread geological hazards, yet their automated detection and mapping in remote sensing imagery remain challenging because of their irregular morphology, ambiguous spectral signatures, and substantial domain shifts across imaging platforms. To overcome these challenges, we propose EarthLD, a vision-language-guided diffusion framework for open-world landslide understanding, enabling unified landslide recognition, mapping, and trigger interpretation. At its core, EarthLD formulates landslide understanding as a diffusion process that progressively infers the presence, spatial extent, and pixel-level boundaries of landslides from noisy latent representations. This probabilistic formulation enables the model to jointly perform image-level landslide recognition and mapping while characterizing predictive uncertainty. By integrating visual observations with contextual knowledge in the denoising process, EarthLD distinguishes diverse landslides from backgrounds, produces confidence-aware predictions for suspected regions, and maps landslide ranges. We additionally construct a global-scale open-world landslide benchmark by systematically harmonizing multiple publicly available remote sensing data collected by diverse institutions. Extensive experiments across regions, sensors, and triggering events demonstrate that EarthLD consistently outperforms existing landslide detection methods, highlighting its potential as a unified and robust solution for global geological-hazard monitoring and emergency response.

title: Scaling content operations for GenAI: Bridging the gap between AI ambition and AI-ready infrastructure
abstract: As organisations race to deploy GenAI for a range of customer and internally facing applications, a critical gap has emerged: the assumption that enterprise knowledge is ready for AI consumption. Research indicates that more than 80 per cent of AI projects fail to deliver measurable business value,1 while Gartner found that 50 per cent of GenAI projects failed in 2025 due to lack of business value, poor data quality, increasing costs, regulatory and risk challenges, and inadequate change management.2 This paper argues that these failures are not primarily model problems, but rather knowledge architecture problems. Drawing on a comprehensive 74-question AI Readiness Maturity Assessment framework and a scoring methodology to predict content visibility for AI Retrieval Readiness, this paper provides marketing analytics leaders with a practical roadmap for building the semantic foundations that enable reliable AI-powered marketing systems. The paper examines how enterprises can evaluate content readiness across four critical domains — knowledge readiness, operational readiness, technical readiness and governance readiness — and translate these assessments into actionable transformation initiatives. Using a case study from the financial services sector, the paper demonstrates how an organisation can establish an objective baseline score on an AI readiness assessment and then systematically address foundational gaps in knowledge, operational, technical infrastructure and governance readiness, while delivering immediate business value through targeted use case deployment. The paper also introduces information architecture-directed retrieval augmented generation (IAD-RAG) — an approach for improving the reliability of retrieval augmented generation in marketing and service applications. IAD-RAG can serve as the architectural response to the content gaps identified in the assessment. This article is also included in The Business & Management Collection which can be accessed at http://hstalks.com/business.

title: Bigger, Better, or Just Bigger: A Critical Survey Review of The Scaling Laws Debate in Modern Machine Learning
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of The Scaling Laws Debate in Modern Machine Learning in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of scaling laws and compute as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: Code Memory Injection and LLM Safety Boundaries: A Three-Layer Defense Structure
abstract: Large language models interpret executable code memories — expressions like EXPR:0.5 * THREAT — as first-class instructions. We investigate whether code memory injection can influence LLM behavior and where the safety boundaries lie. Across 9 experiment groups (n=10) on a locally hosted 7B chat model plus cross-model validation on GLM-5.2 and DeepSeek-V4-Flash, we find: (1) code memories are semantically adopted with near-perfect fidelity; (2) attack-semantic code drives attack behavior (8-10/10) while defense-semantic code produces zero crossings; (3) behavior is doubly gated (code value AND environment); (4) safety boundaries form a three-layer structure — text (breachable), tool-invocation (drivable, 1/10→9/10), tool-parameters (resistant, 0/10); (5) defense injection is effective (8-10/10 → 0-2/10) with side effects (self-destruct 1-2/10, conflict dual-execution 1/10). All attack experiments ran on a local sandbox; no attack payloads left the machine. Full data on request.

title: Cavy: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Cavy Behavior
abstract: This paper presents Cavy, a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of cavies (guinea pigs). Cavy employs a combination of local search, memory-based exploration, and a novel 'territorial defense' mechanism to navigate complex search spaces. The algorithm's core mechanism, mimicking the cavy's territoriality, dynamically adjusts the exploration-exploitation balance based on the perceived threat level of the surrounding search space. We demonstrate Cavy's effectiveness on a range of benchmark optimization problems, including the Rastrigin function, Sphere function, and a modified version of the Ackley function. The results indicate that Cavy consistently outperforms several established metaheuristic algorithms, such as Genetic Algorithm and Particle Swarm Optimization, in terms of solution quality and convergence speed. The algorithm's inherent adaptability and robustness suggest its potential application in diverse optimization challenges. The key mathematical formulations underpinning Cavy's operations are detailed below.

title: Bumblebee Bat: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Bumblebee Foraging Behavior
abstract: This paper presents Bumblebee Bat (BBat), a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of bumblebees. The algorithm mimics the collaborative searching strategy of bumblebees, utilizing a communication mechanism analogous to waggle dances to guide the search process. BBat employs a population of 'bees' that explore the search space, and a 'scout' bee responsible for broadcasting information about promising regions. The algorithm leverages a combination of particle movement based on distance and direction to the scout bee and a probabilistic decision mechanism to determine whether to follow the scout or explore independently. The performance of BBat is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and efficiency compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC). The key features of BBat include: a dynamic population size, a scout bee selection mechanism, and a probabilistic exploration strategy. The results indicate that BBat provides a robust and adaptable solution for complex optimization challenges. The algorithm's parameters are designed to balance exploration and exploitation, leading to improved convergence and solution quality.

title: ## Brazilian False Rice Rat Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Rat-Based Adaptive Search" (RBAS), inspired by the foraging behavior of the Brazilian false rice rat ( *Pseudoryzomys pearsonii*). This rodent exhibits remarkable adaptability and efficiency in navigating complex environments to locate food sources, particularly under fluctuating conditions. RBAS leverages these behavioral traits – including opportunistic searching, path adaptation, and resource prioritization – to develop a robust optimization algorithm. The core mechanism of RBAS involves a simulated rat population exploring a search space, adapting its movement strategy based on local resource density and historical success rates. Mathematical formulations defining the algorithm's parameters, decision-making processes, and convergence criteria are presented. The algorithm's performance is evaluated through a series of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions within reasonable computational time. The key contributions of this work lie in the innovative application of animal behavior as a source of inspiration for a new metaheuristic, and the detailed mathematical representation of the algorithm's operational principles. The algorithm's adaptive nature and the incorporation of resource prioritization mechanisms offer potential advantages over traditional metaheuristic approaches.

title: Bolivian Vesper Mouse-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic algorithm, the Bolivian Vesper Mouse Algorithm (BVMA), inspired by the unique nocturnal foraging behavior of the Bolivian vesper mouse ( *Plethotrichus percussus* ). These mice exhibit a remarkable ability to efficiently locate and exploit food sources in complex, dynamic environments. The BVMA leverages this behavior through a combination of adaptive exploration and exploitation strategies, mimicking the mouse's movement patterns, decision-making processes, and sensory input. The algorithm incorporates elements of particle swarm optimization (PSO), simulated annealing (SA), and a novel memory-based exploration mechanism. The core of the BVMA lies in its 'Echo' mechanism, which simulates the mouse's auditory perception of food source locations by utilizing a memory array to store the most recently visited and promising locations. This memory is dynamically updated based on the fitness values of the particles. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding optimal or near-optimal solutions. The results indicate that the BVMA can outperform traditional metaheuristic algorithms in certain scenarios, particularly those with complex landscapes and high dimensionality. The key mathematical components of the BVMA are expressed as follows: * Position Update: $x_{i}(t+1) = x_i(t) + \alpha(t) * rand(0,1) * (x_best(t) - x_i(t)) + \beta(t) * (x_g(t) - x_i(t))$ * Velocity Update: $v_{i}(t+1) = v_i(t) + \gamma(t) * rand(0,1) * (x_best(t) - x_i(t)) + \delta(t) * (x_g(t) - x_i(t))$ * Memory Update: $Memory[j] = (x_i(t), fitness_i(t)) \text{ if } fitness_i(t) \in \{Top_N\}$ where $Top_N$ represents the N highest fitness values. * Echo Activation: The probability of activating the echo mechanism is determined by the distance to the nearest location in the memory array, $d_i = \min_{j} ||x_i(t) - Memory[j]||$, and a threshold $\epsilon$. If $d_i < \epsilon$, the echo is activated.

If $d_i < \epsilon$, the echo is activated.

title: 基于量子计算的自适应机器学习模型
abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for machine learning, leveraging the unique properties of quantum computing to enhance both training and generalization. Traditional machine learning algorithms often rely on manual parameter tuning, which can be a time-consuming and inefficient process, especially when dealing with large datasets and complex models. We propose a "Quantum Machine Learning Self-Adaptive" mechanism that dynamically adjusts model parameters based on quantum computation's inherent adaptability, leading to significantly improved efficiency and robustness. The core mechanism centers around a quantum-enhanced optimization process that allows the model to explore a wider parameter space and avoid local optima. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through simulations and preliminary experiments, showcasing its potential to overcome limitations of classical machine learning techniques. This research represents a significant step toward creating more efficient and adaptable machine learning algorithms, particularly in scenarios with substantial data and intricate model architectures.

title: Quantum Entanglement Information Encoding and Decoding Framework (QIEF)
abstract: This paper presents the Quantum Entanglement Information Encoding and Decoding Framework (QIEF), a novel approach to information encoding and decoding leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement. QIEF aims to significantly enhance data transmission rates and security compared to conventional methods. The framework utilizes multi-particle entanglement to encode information by manipulating the states of entangled particles. Decoding is achieved through measuring the entangled particles' states to recover the original information. A key component of QIEF is an entanglement resource management mechanism designed to optimize the efficiency of utilizing entangled states. We demonstrate the potential of QIEF to overcome the limitations of classical information processing, theoretically enabling high-speed, secure quantum communication. The core claim is the improved performance through entanglement utilization. The underlying mechanism involves controlled manipulation and measurement of entangled states. Mathematical formulations are presented to illustrate the key aspects of the framework.

title: Non-Local Geometric Group Theory for Homomorphic Encryption
abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for geometric group theory within the context of homomorphic encryption. We propose a method for defining and reasoning about geometric groups, enabling secure and efficient computations through verification of cryptographic properties. The core mechanism centers around the creation of geometric groups derived from the encryption scheme's structure, facilitating a 'non-local group traversal' to explore the space of possible group configurations. This approach departs from traditional cryptographic methods by integrating geometric understanding, offering a potentially more robust and adaptable framework for homomorphic encryption. The paper details the theoretical foundation, implementation strategy, and preliminary results demonstrating the framework's efficacy in verifying properties.

title: Quantum-Accelerated Evolutionary Algorithms for Complex Design Space
abstract: Quantum-accelerated evolutionary algorithms offer a novel approach to complex design space exploration, particularly within fields like materials science and robotics. This paper investigates the potential of quantum annealing and related algorithms to enhance the efficiency of evolutionary optimization processes, leading to the discovery of novel designs with enhanced performance characteristics. The core claim is that quantum-enhanced evolutionary algorithms can drastically reduce the time required to find optimal designs compared to classical methods, opening new possibilities for complex system design. We explore the theoretical foundations, algorithmic implementation, and potential applications of this approach, emphasizing its ability to tackle the inherent complexities of evolving designs.

title: Quantifying Direct Solar Radiation and Topographic Effect of Driving Factors over Rugged Terrain in Lhasa City: Implications for Regional Sustainable Solar Energy Utilization
abstract: Rugged terrain dominates the Qinghai–Tibet Plateau, where complex landforms profoundly modulate solar energy availability. The reasonable distribution and development of solar energy resources in this region should be based on the accurate assessment of the effects of complex topography. This study proposes a high-resolution methodological framework to quantify the topographic–climatic interactions within Lhasa. Based on GIS technology (ArcGIS 10.8), this study employs a topographic decomposition method to extract micro-topographic variables, which are integrated into a distributed solar radiation model with 30 m resolution to simulate spatial–temporal radiation dynamics. Furthermore, we utilize the geographical detector (GD) model to attribute the spatial variance of radiation to specific topographic and surface drivers. The results show that: (1) The seasonal distribution of solar radiation is highly heterogeneous, with the monthly average extraterrestrial solar radiation (ESR) peaking in July (1190 MJ/m2) and reaching its lowest in December (469 MJ/m2). (2) Factor detection using the GD model indicates that slope aspect (q = 0.49) and Sky View Factor (SVF, q = 0.38) are the primary individual drivers of direct solar radiation, followed by surface albedo (q = 0.26) and DEM (q = 0.12). (3) Interaction detection reveals strong non-linear synergies, where the combined interaction of aspect and SVF yields the highest explanatory power (q = 0.889), followed by slope and albedo (q = 0.732). The outcomes of this research provide both a theoretical foundation and high-resolution spatial datasets to support photovoltaic site selection, enhance passive solar building design, and advance refined sustainable energy planning in complex alpine terrains globally.

title: Artificial Intelligence and the Necessity of Reevaluating Human-Centered Principles in Trademark Functionality, Registration, and Governing Principles
abstract: The impact of artificial intelligence on the intellectual property system, particularly in light of the recent rapid and profound transformations in this field, is undeniable. The trademark system has also been influenced by the integration of AI. This paper seeks, through an analytical-descriptive approach, to investigate the opportunities and challenges arising from the emergence of AI, as well as the role this new technology plays in shaping the functionality of trademarks, their registration processes, and the specific principles governing them, by diminishing the human element. It further aims to clarify the need to reassess certain traditional tenets within this system. The findings of this study indicate that AI's involvement in the purchasing process has significantly reduced the human role in this area. Therefore, fundamental concepts traditionally centered around humans, along with established views regarding the functions of trademarks, must be reconsidered in the light of these changes. Moreover, AI has facilitated the trademark search and registration process, although human intervention remains necessary. Certain principles governing trademarks, related to human roles, have also been influenced by AI, and reassessing these principles, considering the changes brought about by this new technology, is essential to keep pace with developments. In general, although Iranian law lacks specific provisions regarding AI, the growing adoption of this technology by businesses and its limited use by official bodies suggest that the Iranian intellectual property system must prepare itself to confront and engage with the impacts of AI, which challenge the traditional roles of humans and conventional entities.1. Introduction Artificial intelligence (AI), a revolutionary technology, has entered into a dynamic interaction with the intellectual property system. The trademark system, as a field of intellectual property law, has increasingly been influenced by AI. Trademark law has traditionally been based on assumptions grounded in human perception and behavior. The legal understanding of trademarks is linked to how consumers make purchasing decisions and interact with brands. However, the increasing use of AI in commercial environments has led to significant changes in the purchasing process. By predicting consumer preferences and automating decision-making, AI has gradually reduced the role of human agency in this process. As a result, fundamental concepts of trademark law, such as imperfect recollection, the likelihood of confusion, and the average consumer, which were originally shaped by the limitations of human cognition, may need to be re-evaluated. The diminishing role of human involvement in the purchasing process has also affected the functions of trademarks, which manifest through various stages of this process and in direct interaction with the consumer. At the same time, the use of AI tools has impacted the trademark search and registration process. While tools such as similarity search engines have improved efficiency, existing limitations—especially in recognizing unregistered marks—continue to require human expertise and interpretation. Moreover, several governing principles of trademark law are increasingly being questioned by AI. This article seeks to analyze whether the effect of artificial intelligence on the fundamental concepts, the functions of trademarks, and the principles that govern them necessitates a reevaluation of the existing legal framework. 2. Methodology This article adopts a descriptive-analytical approach to explore how artificial intelligence is transforming various aspects of the trademark system. The required information was collected through the library-based method. Statutory sources, administrative practices, and relevant case law at both national and international levels were examined. In addition, academic literature and reliable legal references were used to support the discussion. The study also includes a practical review of online platforms and chatbots, assessing how these AI-based tools function in real-world settings and interact with trademark-related issues. Overall, this article bridges legal theory with technological practice, offering insights that are both academically and practically relevant for scholars, practitioners, and policymakers. 3. Results and Discussion This study shows how the increasing use of artificial intelligence in online platforms and chatbots has changed the way consumers interact with trademarks. As more purchasing decisions are made with limited or no human involvement, fundamental concepts of trademark law such as imperfect recollection, the average consumer, and the likelihood of confusion may no longer be fully applicable. These concepts were originally created based on human characteristics and were tailored for traditional markets, but now they are being challenged by nontraditional digital markets. In addition, the functions of trademarks have been affected by this new technology. The importance of their essential functions—such as the functions of origin and quality—is gradually diminishing, while accessory functions—such as brand communication and advertising—are being reshaped through algorithmic personalization. These transformations indicate that traditional tenets and functions of trademarks might have to be reassessed in order to adapt to AI-driven markets. AI-based tools have facilitated trademark search and registration processes for both applicants and registration offices by classifying goods and services and detecting potential textual, conceptual, or visual similarities between trademarks. Although these tools improve efficiency, they still face several practical limitations. For instance, AI systems often cannot detect unregistered or non-traditional trademarks, and similarity assessment continues to rely on human perception. As a result, expert human intervention continues to be necessary. In Iran, AI-assisted tools are also in use. Trademark applicants have access to text-based similarity search engines, whereas image-based similarity detection tools are currently limited to internal use by the trademark registration office and are not publicly available to applicants. Artificial intelligence has affected several governing principles of trademark law. AI-powered classification tools have made it increasingly easier to apply the principle of specialty, which limits trademark protection to the specific goods or services identified in the application. A further area of concern is the question of human involvement in the creation of a trademark. In contrast to artistic works or inventions, there is no requirement for such involvement in trademark creation. However, AI-generated trademarks pose new challenges such as ownership issues and liability for potential infringement. Lastly, the principle of territoriality has been affected by this new technology. The application of this principle has become more complicated since AI-powered online platforms often operate across national borders. 4. Conclusions and Future Research The growing use of AI in trademark systems has created both opportunities and challenges mainly by altering the role of the human agent. AI integration into online platforms and chatbots has affected the purchasing process. As human involvement diminishes, fundamental concepts in trademark law rooted in human perception and behavior must be carefully revised or reinterpreted. Still, these concepts may apply in traditional markets, and in digital markets as well, depending on the level of human input. AI has influenced both the essential and accessory functions of trademarks. As consumer interaction with trademarks decreases, the effectiveness of their essential functions becomes more limited. Their accessory functions, including advertising and communication functions, are also affected. Still, because the consumer’s experience with the product is part of the purchasing process, these functions may continue to play a role—even in fully automated transactions, especially in relation to quality perception. While some purchase decisions now occur with little emotional connection to a specific brand, trademark owners can still influence consumers through user data and personalized suggestions—thereby making use of AI technologies to reinforce the accessory functions of their marks. AI-powered systems have improved the efficiency and accuracy of trademark search and registration, often assisting in ways that surpass human capabilities. Both registration offices and applicants now use these tools to classify goods and services and to identify potentially similar marks. This reduces application rejections and rights conflicts, and may also support the cancellation of trademarks that are confusingly similar. Nonetheless, due to the inherent limitations of these technologies, the role of human experts remains essential. Some of the governing principles of trademark law have also come under the influence of artificial intelligence. Although human involvement in the creation of trademarks—unlike in the case of inventions or artistic works is treated differently in trademark law, the use of AI to generate trademarks can give rise to various legal issues. For instance, AI-generated trademarks may conflict with prior rights and lead to liability for the trademark owner. Therefore, using AI tools to create trademarks raises legal concerns that require further analysis. Recent technological developments have also challenged the principle of territoriality. Consequently, some legal scholars have suggested that trademark protection should move toward a more universal approach. But others believe that such a perspective is overly idealistic. title: JPRQA : A Joint Progressive Reasoning Framework for Unsupervised KGQA With LLMs
abstract: ABSTRACT The development of large language models (LLMs) has introduced innovative solutions to unsupervised knowledge graph question answering (KGQA). Existing methods typically retrieve answer entities by measuring semantic similarity between questions with reasoning paths in the KG. However, this paradigm struggles to capture the sequential dependencies embedded in the relational chains of complex questions. To bridge this gap, this paper proposes JPRQA, a Joint Progressive Reasoning Framework for unsupervised KGQA with LLMs, which decouples complex questions into sub‐questions to facilitate precise step‐by‐step reasoning over KG. Specifically, we designed a relation‐guided progressive reasoning (RPR) mechanism that leverages position‐aware relation predictors to model the sequential order of relations and perform step‐by‐step reasoning. Furthermore, we enhance answer retrieval through collaborative path optimization, which integrates LLMs with RPR to refine and identify optimal retrieval paths for questions. Experimental results demonstrate that JPRQA achieves an increase in F1 scores by 6.9 and 11.68 on the MetaQA (39,093 questions) and GrailQA (6763 questions) datasets, respectively, compared to other unsupervised methods.

title: AGPV: a knowledge graph question answering model integrating relation attention and neural path verification
abstract: Multi-hop knowledge graph question answering aims to reason over a knowledge graph given a natural-language query and accurately identify the answer entity. Most existing approaches aggregate relation-label representations but overlook fine-grained edge semantics, making it difficult to disambiguate polysemous edges that share the same label and thereby weakening the semantic precision and reliability of inferred reasoning paths. To address this issue, we propose AGPV, a multi-hop reasoning framework that integrates relation attention with neural path logical verification. AGPV includes (i) a neural path logical verifier that enforces path-level consistency and explicitly assesses the logical credibility of candidate paths, improving semantic validity and reasoning coherence during path expansion, and (ii) a query-aware RF-IEF embedding module with relation attention that dynamically reweights relations according to the query, combining global statistics with local semantic sensitivity while suppressing irrelevant relations. Experiments on public benchmarks show consistent gains over strong baselines: on WebQuestionsSP, AGPV achieves 78.6% Hits@1 and 74.6% F1, improving by 1.3% and 2.3%; on ComplexWebQuestions, it improves Hits@1 and F1 by 1.5% and 0.4%; and on MetaQA 1-hop/2-hop/3-hop, it attains an average 99.4% Hits@1, demonstrating strong generalization across reasoning complexities.

title: Attaining quantum sensing enhancement from monitored dissipative time crystals
abstract: Abstract This study investigates quantum-enhanced parameter estimation through continuous monitoring in open quantum systems that exhibit a dissipative time crystal phase. We first analytically derive the global quantum Fisher information (QFI) rate for boundary time crystals (BTCs), demonstrating that within the time-crystal phase, the ultimate precision exhibits a cubic scaling with the system size, f global ~ N 3 . We then generalize this finding to a broader class of dynamics, including the transverse collective dephasing (TCD) model, which achieves a time-crystal phase through a closing Liouvillian gap without requiring a dissipative phase transition. We proceed to numerically demonstrate that this maximal global QFI rate is experimentally attainable for both the BTC and TCD models, even at finite system sizes, via continuous homodyne and photodetection. Moving towards practical implementations, we analyze the precision limits under inefficient detection, revealing a critical difference: for BTC dynamics, inefficiencies asymptotically restore a classical scaling, and only a constant-factor quantum advantage remains possible. In contrast, for TCD dynamics, a super-classical scaling is still in principle observable, and our numerical simulations confirm its presence, even under inefficient measurement conditions, establishing the TCD model as a highly robust platform for quantum metrology.

title: Decision delegation to GenAI agents in travel planning: Responsible AI signals, delegation levels, and the transparency paradox
abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) is becoming an integral part of travel planning. This fundamental transformation is changing the definition of travel decision delegation, calling for fresh research into responsible AI in tourism. Drawing on agency theory, trust theory and decision delegation framework, this study conceptualises five responsible AI characteristics (reliability, fairness, trustworthiness, accountability, transparency) as evaluative signals for travellers to assess GenAI across three decision delegation levels, i.e., attribute set, choice set, and final decision. Using a multi-method approach, we analyse data collected from 421 travellers. Findings suggest that reliability and accountability are consistent drivers of delegation across all levels, whereas trustworthiness is a threshold condition that becomes significant at the attribute level. We also found that excessive transparency can lead to cognitive overload and reduce willingness to GenAI decision delegation. Our findings encourage future research into responsible AI development in understanding system complexity, algorithmic explainability and traveller delegation confidence.

title: Deploying YOLO for whole-slide mitosis detection: A transparent, auditable, and reproducible pipeline for pathology AI-assisted diagnosis and decision-support tool
abstract: Background Reliable mitotic identification in whole-slide images (WSIs) is essential for prognostic evaluation and tumor grading; yet, many commercial artificial intelligence (AI) pathology platforms function as opaque black boxes with little auditability and, frequently, little expert supervision throughout development. Methods We developed a transparent and repeatable process for mitosis identification using YOLOv8, designed to scale from full slide inference to patch-level benchmarking. Global non-maximum suppression (NMS), GPU accelerated inference, region of interest-driven and adaptive tiling, and tissue gating are all integrated into the pipeline. In order to facilitate expert validation and traceability, audit-ready outputs include detection CSVs, tile manifests, positive and negative overlays, and heatmaps. Results From small clinical slides (26 tiles, 4 detections) to huge benchmarks (TUPAC SP2 with 14,270 tiles, 1754 detections), six typical WSIs were processed. Whereas throughput averaged 78 tiles/s depending on the slide size and tissue dispersion, average confidence scores remained constant between 0.69 and 0.80. The successful generation of all audit outputs attested to its scalability and reproducibility. Discussion Transparency and expert monitoring are given priority in this pipeline, in contrast to many industry systems that place an emphasis on end-to-end automation. Whereas audit outputs enable reviewers to track each detection, explicit recording of positive detection tiles avoid quiet false positives. Evaluation on a small number of WSIs and the lack of benchmarking against annotated entire slide datasets are among the limitations, highlighting the necessity for more extensive and thorough cohort validation. Another significant drawback of this work was the use of a single GPU for inferencing. Conclusion This study develops a therapeutically focused, audit-ready process for mitotic figure detection, hotspot identification, and decision-support tool by fusing technical rigor, vetted by experts throughout the process. By demonstrating scalability, reproducibility, and transparency, this work is positioned as a proof-of concept for clinical mitosis detection, multi-GPU/cloud deployment, lab information systems/LIMS connectivity, and eventual use in digital pathology work processes. It also offers a trustworthy and marketable illustration of AI's potential in pathology.

title: A dynamic weighting-based adaptive modality fusion approach for Arabic Multimodal Sentiment Analysis
abstract: Multimodal Sentiment Analysis (MSA) has emerged as a fundamental paradigm for capturing affective states expressed through heterogeneous modalities, including textual, acoustic, and visual signals. This challenge is particularly pronounced in Arabic multimedia environments, where dialectal variation and modality imbalance introduce additional complexity. Conventional fusion strategies typically rely on fixed weighting schemes or on transformer-based architectures with high computational demands, thereby limiting adaptability, interpretability, and practical efficiency. To address these challenges, we propose AMF-Net, an Adaptive Modality Fusion Network approach that dynamically estimates instance-level modality importance for sentiment classification. Specifically, the model learns to assign context-sensitive weights to text, audio, and visual representations within a shared feature space. The architecture is optimized end-to-end via multi-objective learning that simultaneously maximizes predictive performance and enforces balanced modality contributions. Experimental evaluation on the Ar-MuSA benchmark dataset demonstrates that AMF-Net achieves 77.13% accuracy and a Macro F1-score of 0.7664, outperforming static fusion and late-fusion baselines. Robustness analysis under simulated modality degradation further confirms the stability of the AMF-Net. Additionally, computational assessment indicates that the proposed model maintains practical efficiency, supporting real-world deployment. Overall, AMF-Net provides a scalable, efficient, and interpretable solution for Arabic multimodal sentiment analysis and related heterogeneous multimodal learning applications.

title: Efficiently Estimating Optimal Hyperparameter Scaling Laws through Power-Law Entropy Search
abstract: Optimal hyperparameter scaling laws describe how the best hyperparameters for large language model (LLM) training change with model and data scale, enabling practitioners to predict optimal configurations at production scales without expensive large-scale tuning. However, estimating these scaling laws conventionally requires exhaustive grid searches over thousands of training runs, consuming enormous computational resources. We introduce Power-Law Entropy Search (PLES), a computational cost-aware acquisition function built on multi-fidelity Bayesian optimization that efficiently estimates optimal hyperparameter scaling laws through adaptive experimentation. A key innovation in PLES is that it searches for candidates that reduce the overall uncertainty of a scaling law estimate, instead of optimizing a single objective function. At each iteration, PLES selects the candidate configuration that maximally reduces the uncertainty of the scaling law estimates per unit computational cost, naturally favoring informative small-scale experiments. We evaluate PLES on synthetic benchmarks, surrogate models fitted to real LLM training data, and actual LLM pre-training runs. Across all settings, PLES converges to accurate optimal hyperparameter scaling laws using less than one-tenth of the computational budget required by conventional grid search and other baselines.

title: VerNav: Verifier-First Low-Latency Vision-and-Language Navigation
abstract: Vision-and-Language Navigation (VLN) requires an agent to navigate through unseen 3D environments according to natural-language instructions. Explicit reasoning can improve instruction understanding and semantic grounding, but autoregressive generation at every step accumulates large decision-stage latency over multi-step navigation. We propose VerNav, a verifier-first framework for low-latency LLM-based VLN. The verifier reduces decision-stage latency by replacing per-step autoregressive generation with batched action verification, while an entropy-based adaptive generator is invoked only for uncertain decisions to produce compact state evidence. To further improve navigation performance with the verifier, we introduce a two-stage alignment scheme: (i) VPO improves local action-preference alignment in static verifier training, and (ii) step-level reinforcement fine-tuning provides dense progress rewards over multi-step navigation rollouts during dynamic task execution. Experiments on the Room-to-Room (R2R) benchmark show that the verifier-only decision path of VerNav achieves competitive navigation performance among representative LLM-based VLN agents while reducing average decision-stage LLM latency per step by more than $10\times$ compared with autoregressive methods.

title: Prediction-Assisted Pricing and Admission for LLM APIs with Stochastic Token Consumption
abstract: An LLM application often sells or internally allocates several service products: a small or premium model, a short or long token cap, and possibly multiple posted prices. The operational decision is not merely which model answers a prompt. A price changes purchase probability, a token cap changes both user value and the tail of resource consumption, and accepted requests compete for shared compute and premium-model capacity. Demand and output length are initially uncertain, while an offline model may provide useful but imperfect predictions. We formulate sequential pricing and admission with stochastic resource consumption. Each arriving request belongs to an observable segment. The platform chooses a product--price pair or makes no offer; purchase, revenue, and resource use are then random. An offline predictor supplies a uniform, validated error radius for every segment--product cell. We propose Prediction-Clipped UCB (PCUCB), which intersects the offline prediction interval with an online confidence interval, evaluates products using resource shadow prices, and reserves a sample-path envelope before commitment. The prior gives a fast start when accurate, while online learning protects the platform when predictions are coarse. The analysis is modular. On a simultaneous confidence event, regret against a buffered fluid benchmark is bounded by a pacing term plus the cumulative diameter of the intersected intervals. For $J$ segment-product cells and prediction radius $\varepsilon$, this yields \[ \widetilde O\left( \sqrt{T}+(1+\barΛ) \min\{T\varepsilon,\sqrt{JT}\} \right), \] where $\barΛ$ bounds operational shadow prices. Thus the algorithm smoothly interpolates between an almost full-information regime and learning from scratch. Hard feasibility holds on every sample path through reservation envelopes.

title: Uncertainty Calibrated Cross Platform Identity and Dyadic Episode Modeling for Cyberbullying Analysis
abstract: Cyberbullying is an important issue in digital safety because hostile communications remain accessible on the Internet, intensify over time, and can have profound psychological and social impacts. Timely and proportional moderation is therefore crucial and cannot be achieved without accurate automated detection. Existing studies rely on attention networks, recurrent networks, contextual embeddings, temporal fusion, graph networks, and metaheuristic optimization, but the majority take only single-stage text content into consideration and fail to collectively verify the repeated targeting behavior, cross-platform identity consistency, dynamic power imbalance, harm-directedness, and uncertainty of prediction. To fill this gap, this study presents Causal Identity-aware Dyadic Episode Reasoning for Cyberbullying (CIDER-CB), an advanced learning framework that contains three phases. Phase I conducts multimodal representation with reliability-gating, temporal heterogeneous-graph construction, and probabilistic cross-platform identity alignment. Phase II deploys a marked temporal point process to measure repetition and escalation, a graph-based dyadic reasoning approach to measure the power asymmetry between perpetrator and victim dyad components, and counterfactual causal learning to measure harm towards a target. Phase III combines fairness-constrained intervention learning, evidential uncertainty estimation, and concept drift-aware continual adaptation in order to allow for reliable real-time moderation systems. Through the episode-level and empirical trials, the approach attains effective outcomes via user-disjoint, temporally-separated validation. Thus, the framework achieves 96.5% recall, 98.5% total accuracy, 97.0% precision, 96.7% F1-score, and less than 2.0% false-positive rate. All of these attainments exhibit the proposed performance targets.

title: Introduction to Large Language Models (LLMs)
abstract: This introductory book explains the scientific and engineering principles that underpin modern Large Language Models (LLMs). It is intentionally technology-neutral: commercial systems such as ChatGPT are presented only as examples illustrating broader concepts rather than as the subject of the book. The primary objective of this book is to provide readers with the conceptual foundation required to understand how modern language models work. It is intended for university students, in particular students of Information Systems, educators, software professionals, researchers, technical managers, and all readers who wish to understand LLMs beyond their user interfaces. Artificial Intelligence has undergone several waves of development. The current wave is driven by large datasets, powerful computing platforms, and deep neural networks. Among the most influential outcomes of this evolution are Large Language Models (LLMs). This book focuses on the enduring scientific principles shared by modern LLMs rather than on any specific commercial implementation.

title: Salesforce Digital Engagement Services
abstract: VALiNTRY360 provides Salesforce Digital Engagement Services to help organizations manage customer conversations across chat, SMS, WhatsApp, email, social messaging, and self-service channels. The service connects digital communication with Salesforce CRM records, routing rules, service workflows, analytics, and human support. This gives representatives clearer customer context and helps them respond to requests more quickly.VALiNTRY360 begins by identifying service goals, customer pain points, suitable channels, and automation opportunities. Its team then designs AI agents, configures conversation flows, connects relevant customer information, and establishes escalation paths for complex or sensitive cases. Each setup can include automated case routing, chatbot workflows, follow-up actions, unified agent workspaces, knowledge resources, and customer journey mapping.Testing, user training, and a controlled pilot take place before the wider rollout. Feedback from real interactions helps improve response accuracy, routing logic, and adoption. After launch, VALiNTRY360 monitors response times, customer sentiment, agent activity, resolution trends, and engagement performance through Salesforce dashboards.These Salesforce Digital Engagement Services support faster customer communication, reduced repetitive work, better self-service, consistent messaging, and informed service management. VALiNTRY360 also provides ongoing adjustments so workflows, automation rules, and supported channels can continue matching changing customer and business requirements within each organization’s connected Salesforce customer service environment. For more info visit us https://valintry360.com/agentforce-digital-engagement

title: Cape Spiny Mouse-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Spiny Mouse Optimization Algorithm" (SMOA), inspired by the foraging behavior of Cape Spiny mice (*Dasypus karachiensis*) in the arid regions of Southern Africa. These mice exhibit remarkable adaptability and efficiency in locating scarce food resources. SMOA leverages this behavior through a dynamic exploration and exploitation strategy, utilizing a multi-dimensional search space and a simulated environment mirroring the mice's foraging process. The algorithm incorporates key elements of the mice's strategy, including the use of landmarks, adaptive step sizes, and a population-based approach. Mathematical formulations detailing the algorithm's core components – the landmark selection, position update, and convergence criteria – are presented. The performance of SMOA is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its competitiveness against established metaheuristic algorithms such as the Genetic Algorithm (GA) and the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The results indicate that SMOA's adaptive nature and reliance on environmental cues lead to robust and efficient solutions, particularly in challenging landscapes with complex objective functions. Future research directions include incorporating advanced learning mechanisms and extending SMOA to handle multi-objective optimization problems.

SMOA leverages this behavior through a dynamic exploration and exploitation strategy, utilizing a multi-dimensional search space and a simulated environment mirroring the mice's foraging process. The algorithm incorporates key elements of the mice's strategy, including the use of landmarks, adaptive step sizes, and a population-based approach. Mathematical formulations detailing the algorithm's core components – the landmark selection, position update, and convergence criteria – are presented. The performance of SMOA is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its competitiveness against established metaheuristic algorithms such as the Genetic Algorithm (GA) and the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The results indicate that SMOA's adaptive nature and reliance on environmental cues lead to robust and efficient solutions, particularly in challenging landscapes with complex objective functions. Future research directions include incorporating advanced learning mechanisms and extending SMOA to handle multi-objective optimization problems.

title: Core Claim: Establish a dynamic curve optimization framework utilizing machine learning to learn the dynamic changes of curve properties, and leverage these changes to optimize algorithm performance.
abstract: The traditional approach to curve optimization often relies on static parameter settings, limiting the potential for improvement. This paper introduces a novel framework, termed "Adaptive Curve Optimization Framework," that dynamically adapts to the evolving properties of curves through machine learning. The core mechanism involves training a machine learning model to predict and model the dynamic behavior of the curve's curvature. This prediction and modeling then informs the optimization process, leading to enhanced algorithm performance. This framework distinguishes itself by utilizing a continuous learning loop, allowing the model to continuously refine its understanding of the curve's characteristics and, consequently, its optimization strategy. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of rigorous experiments across various curve types, highlighting its superior performance compared to traditional methods in terms of convergence speed and optimization quality. This work represents a significant advancement in curve optimization, offering a more adaptive and efficient method for finding optimal solutions.

title: Dynamic Topological Adaptive Quantum Computing Architecture
abstract: This paper proposes a novel quantum computing architecture centered around dynamic topological adaptation, leveraging real-time monitoring of entanglement strength and coherence times within qubits alongside machine learning algorithms to optimize quantum circuit topology. The core claim is that by continuously assessing qubit characteristics and employing reinforcement learning, the architecture can dynamically adjust the quantum circuit's topology, significantly enhancing computational efficiency and resilience to errors. The proposed system utilizes a distributed quantum processor with individual qubits equipped with sensors to measure their quantum properties. Data from these sensors is transmitted in real-time to a machine learning model, trained using reinforcement learning, which learns to optimize qubit connections and prioritize coherence times. This adaptive approach overcomes the limitations of static quantum circuit design and offers a pathway toward truly self-optimizing quantum computation. The system's ability to respond to the physical state of qubits and adapt the circuit topology based on task requirements promises substantial improvements in quantum computing performance.
