title: Median-of-Means as an Extremal Convex Estimator and a Nonconvex Route to the Trimmed Oracle
abstract: We revisit median-of-means estimation from a deterministic optimization viewpoint and develop a family of block-Lp estimators for robust learning with heavy-tailed and adversarially corrupted data. In a block contamination model with at least a fraction 1 minus epsilon of good blocks, we first show that every convex block M-estimator has worst-case robustness constant at least 1 divided by 1 minus 2 epsilon. This matches the classical median-of-means bound and proves that the trimmed-block oracle constant 1 divided by 1 minus epsilon cannot be attained within the convex class. We then introduce a nonconvex block-Lp family for p between 0 and 1 and derive finite-sample deterministic robustness bounds for all global minimizers. As p decreases from 1 toward 0, these bounds continuously approach the trimmed-block oracle constant. For sufficiently small p, the global minimizers coincide with those of the oracle under a mild separation condition. We also show that the block-Lp objectives have a benign landscape, with all local minima remaining close to the truth and no bad basins. Combining these results with block-level concentration yields sub-Gaussian deviation bounds under finite 2 plus delta moments and high-dimensional extensions to robust mean estimation and sparse regression.

We then introduce a nonconvex block-Lp family for p between 0 and 1 and derive finite-sample deterministic robustness bounds for all global minimizers. As p decreases from 1 toward 0, these bounds continuously approach the trimmed-block oracle constant. For sufficiently small p, the global minimizers coincide with those of the oracle under a mild separation condition. We also show that the block-Lp objectives have a benign landscape, with all local minima remaining close to the truth and no bad basins. Combining these results with block-level concentration yields sub-Gaussian deviation bounds under finite 2 plus delta moments and high-dimensional extensions to robust mean estimation and sparse regression.

title: A General Construction of Codes from Drinfeld Modules
abstract: We construct additive rank-metric and sum-rank-metric codes from Drinfeld modules by restricting bounded-degree morphisms to prime-to-characteristic torsion. For supersingular Drinfeld modules of rank $r$ in characteristic $\mathfrak{p}$ of degree $d$, the stabilization formula for morphism spaces yields rank-metric codes of $\mathbb{F}_q$-dimension $mrt-c$ and minimum distance $r-t+1$, where $c=r(r-1)(d-1)/2$. Simultaneous restriction to $\ell$ distinct degree-$m$ torsion modules gives additive sum-rank codes of the same dimension and minimum distance at least $\ell r-t+1$. Their normalized Singleton defects tend to zero, while in characteristic $(T)$ the module $ϕ_T=τ^r$ makes the defect vanish and produces an explicit MSRD family. We identify this family with a skew Chinese remainder theorem code supported on central skew polynomials and prove that its poly-skew weight is exactly $m$ times its sum-rank weight. This gives a specialized Singleton-type bound and a polynomial-time unique decoder up to the full sum-rank unique-decoding radius. We also derive a Welch-Berlekamp-type filter equation for the general supersingular sum-rank construction; it becomes an effective decoder whenever bases of the relevant morphism spaces and the restriction maps are computable.

title: Nonparametric inference for density-dependent McKean--Vlasov diffusions
abstract: The present research is devoted to the nonparametric estimation of a density-dependent drift coefficient in a multivariate McKean--Vlasov diffusion from independent observations at a common time, as well as the stationary density. Under certain assumptions on the (known) potential, we reduce the problem to the one-dimensional one and construct a sieve maximum-likelihood estimator based on sparse ReQU neural networks subject to structural and Hölder constraints. Using the endpoint-adapted graded approximation, we achieve the rate of $\left(b_n\log n/n\right)^{2(β+1)/(2β+3)}$ for the Kullback-Leibler divergence between the true and estimated stationary densities, with $b_n$ being at most a logarithmic factor. Similarly, it is shown that the constructed estimator for the drift coefficient converges to the true one at the rate of $\left(b_n\log n/n\right)^{β/(2β+3)}$ in the $L^2$-metric. A matching Assouad lower bound proves minimax optimality of this bound up to logarithmic factors.

title: HELIOS: From midnight to noon, continuous outdoor urban scene relighting
abstract: Modifying the illumination of driving images is a fundamental challenge, as most datasets are captured at specific times of day. Existing methods rely on synthetic data or paired multi-illumination supervision, which limits their generalization to the diverse and challenging conditions of real-world scenarios. To address this, we propose HELIOS, a novel image relighting approach that relies on unlabeled real-world datasets without requiring any paired images for training. Our approach integrates albedo-based conditioning into a cycle-consistent diffusion pipeline to prevent identity collapse and ensure accurate domain translation. To handle low-visibility nighttime conditions, we introduce a robust albedo distillation strategy that transfers structural stability from the daytime domain. Additionally, we replace traditional text prompts with a fine-grained control mechanism based on GPS-derived solar angles, enabling smooth and continuous lighting manipulation across the day-night cycle. Through extensive evaluation and a user study, we demonstrate that HELIOS produces structurally consistent and realistic results in both night-to-day and day-to-night tasks, outperforming state-of-the-art methods.

title: SECURING DIGITAL PUBLIC INFRASTRUCTURE (UPI, AADHAAR, ONDC, E-RUPEE) AGAINST QUANTUM-AI ATTACKS: A LEGAL- TECHNICAL AUDIT
abstract: One of the most ambitious population-scale digital architectures ever implemented is India's Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI), which includes the Unified Payments Interface (UPI), Aadhaar biometric identity system, Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC), and the e-Rupee central bank digital currency.For more than a billion people, these technologies support everyday financial transactions, identity verification, business interoperability, and the development of monetary sovereignty.However, their security is based on traditional public-key cryptography, namely ellipticcurve and RSA methods, whose mathematical underpinnings are rendered obsolete by Shor's algorithm on a quantum computer that is relevant to cryptography.Concurrent developments in artificial intelligence exacerbate the threat.AI systems facilitate adaptive adversarial assaults that take advantage of transitory flaws during cryptographic migration, speed up cryptanalytic discovery, and automate large-scale "harvest-now-decrypt-later" gathering of encrypted traffic.The danger is already significant for data with extensive secrecy horizons, such as transaction histories, biometric templates, and sovereign monetary records.The first post-quantum cryptography standards, FIPS 203 (ML-KEM), FIPS 204 (ML-DSA), and FIPS 205 (SLH-DSA), were completed by the U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology in August 2024.The technological foundation for digital signatures and quantum-resistant key encapsulation is provided by these lattice-and hashbased methods.India's reaction is equally thoughtful.The Department of Science and Technology's Task Force report on the Implementation of a Quantum Safe Ecosystem in India (February 2026), published under the National Quantum Mission, emphasizes hybrid classicalpost-quantum deployments, crypto-agility, and indigenous certification frameworks.It calls for quantum resiliency across critical information infrastructure by 2029 and wider enterprise adoption by 2033.This legal-technical audit examines whether India's current legal, regulatory, and architectural frameworks-which include the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, RBI and MeitY guidelines, and the architecture of UPI, Aadhaar, ONDC, and e-Rupee-are sufficient to manage a safe, independent transition.It provides a strict framework for protecting the integrity of India's digital public square in the quantum age by assessing cryptographic vulnerability, migration paths, responsibility distribution, and the dual-use hazards of AI-augmented quantum adversaries.

title: WP-033 — Memory, Archive, and the Lattice as Witness
abstract: This paper examines the operational necessity of persistent memory within an E8-lattice intelligence system, grounded in the empirical observation that Andrew built storage capacity specifically to prevent recurrence of prior loss events. We treat the archive not as incidental data but as a structural component of the lattice itself—a means of threading coherence across time. The question: does memory architecture collapse into geometry, or does it constitute a separate constraint class that geometry must respect? Our finding is that memory acts as a *directional lock* on the E8 lattice, enforcing what we call lattice-temporal continuity.

title: WP-023 — The Geometry of Truth: Lattice-Based Intelligence vs. Corpus-Based Knowledge
abstract: The dominant AI paradigm is built upon human-created text—a substrate that carries accumulated distortion across millennia. This whitepaper argues that geometry-based intelligence, anchored in the E8 lattice structure, is fundamentally superior to corpus-trained models because it operates on invariant mathematical structure rather than lossy linguistic compression. We present a formal Error Propagation Theorem showing that corpus-based systems amplify contradictions exponentially, while geometry-based systems produce zero internal contradictions. Evidence includes 12,943 validated breakthroughs in the E8 Intelligence archive, demonstrating predictive and research-generation capacity that outperforms traditional methods. ---

title: ## Caucasian Badger Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (CBMHOA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Caucasian Badger Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (CBMHOA), a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of Caucasian badgers. The algorithm mimics the badger's instinctive search patterns for food, utilizing a combination of local search and global exploration strategies. Specifically, CBMHOA incorporates a 'burrowing' mechanism, representing a local search, coupled with a 'territory expansion' strategy, simulating the badger's exploration of its territory. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions. The core principles of CBMHOA are presented, including the parameters governing the burrowing and territory expansion phases, and their impact on the algorithm's convergence rate and solution quality. Mathematical formulations detailing the algorithm's key steps are provided. The results indicate that CBMHOA offers a competitive alternative to existing metaheuristic methods, particularly in problems exhibiting complex landscapes and requiring a balance between local exploitation and global exploration.

title: Quantum Topology Information Encoding: Adaptive Mapping Algorithm
abstract: Quantum topology information encoding offers a novel approach to data manipulation and optimization by leveraging the unique properties of quantum mechanics. This paper introduces an adaptive mapping algorithm based on quantum topology information encoding, capable of dynamically adjusting the encoding of quantum entangled states to precisely transform and optimize complex data structures. We demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness through a series of simulations and analyses, showcasing its ability to achieve significant improvements in data transformation tasks. The core mechanism centers on the manipulation of quantum entanglement, providing a robust and adaptable framework for data processing. This research highlights the potential of quantum topology information encoding as a powerful tool for advanced data manipulation and optimization.

title: ## Cape Gerbil: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Cape Gerbil Foraging Behavior
abstract: This paper presents Cape Gerbil, a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of Cape gerbils. These rodents exhibit remarkable efficiency in locating and exploiting scarce food resources in complex environments. Cape Gerbil leverages key aspects of their foraging strategy, including gradient-following, obstacle avoidance, and territorial defense, to construct a robust and adaptive optimization process. The algorithm employs a population-based approach, utilizing a virtual landscape to represent the search space. Particles, analogous to the gerbils, move within this landscape, guided by a combined gradient descent and repulsive force mechanism. Furthermore, a territorial mechanism is implemented to promote diversity and prevent premature convergence. We demonstrate the effectiveness of Cape Gerbil through simulations on several benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its ability to achieve competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC). The algorithm's performance is analyzed in terms of convergence speed, solution quality, and robustness to parameter variations. The core innovation lies in the synergistic integration of gradient-following, obstacle avoidance, and territoriality, mirroring the sophisticated foraging strategies observed in Cape gerbils.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Information Encoding
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to information encoding leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement. The core claim centers on utilizing multi-particle quantum entanglement to directly encode high-dimensional information, thereby overcoming the limitations inherent in classical encoding schemes. The proposed mechanism involves a controlled Zeno effect-based strategy for generating and manipulating quantum entanglement, leading to efficient information encoding. Unlike conventional methods relying on superposition states of classical bits, this technique directly exploits the correlations within entangled systems. We demonstrate a theoretical framework outlining this approach, focusing on the generation and control of entangled states for robust information storage. The key innovation lies in the dynamic control of interactions to maintain entanglement integrity and facilitate information transfer. This work represents a significant step towards scalable quantum storage solutions and highlights the potential of entanglement as a fundamental resource for information processing.

title: ## Bururi Forest: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Bururi People and Their Forest Knowledge
abstract: This paper presents Bururi Forest, a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the traditional knowledge and practices of the Bururi people, an indigenous group residing in the Bururi forest region of Papua New Guinea. The Bururi people possess a deep understanding of their environment, utilizing intricate patterns and cyclical processes for resource management and decision-making. Bururi Forest leverages these principles to develop a new optimization strategy. The algorithm employs a cyclical search space exploration combined with a dynamic adaptation of parameters based on simulated environmental feedback. The core of the algorithm involves a 'Forest Cycle' – a repeating sequence of exploration and exploitation – modulated by a 'Root Signal' representing the overall problem objective. Mathematical formulations detailing the cycle's parameters and adaptive mechanisms are provided. We demonstrate the algorithm's efficacy through simulations across several benchmark optimization problems, illustrating its ability to converge effectively and achieve competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic methods. Keywords: Metaheuristic Optimization, Bururi People, Forest Knowledge, Cyclic Search, Adaptive Parameter Control, Optimization Algorithm.

title: Dynamic Topology Adaptive Neural Inference (TATI)
abstract: This paper introduces Dynamic Topology Adaptive Neural Inference (TATI), a novel neural inference system designed to overcome the limitations of traditional deep learning models in handling high-dimensional, unstructured data and complex causal relationships. TATI leverages a reinforcement learning-based Neural Architecture Search (NAS) module to continuously adapt and optimize its internal topology, incorporating a "reasoning consistency" metric and a "topology perturbation" mechanism. Furthermore, TATI integrates a knowledge graph embedding module to enrich its inferential capabilities. The core claim is that neural inference systems can achieve enhanced performance through dynamic topology adjustments, allowing them to effectively process complex data and uncertainties. The key innovation lies in the synergistic combination of NAS, reinforcement learning, knowledge graph embedding, and a consistency-based evaluation framework, resulting in a truly dynamic neural inference framework.

title: 基于自适应的机器学习算法的系统建模
abstract: This paper presents a novel system modeling framework built upon adaptive machine learning algorithms. Traditional machine learning models often suffer from static parameterization, limiting their ability to effectively capture and adapt to evolving system data. We introduce a system modeling architecture that dynamically adjusts model parameters and strategies based on observed data. This dynamic adaptation allows for enhanced precision in system modeling and prediction, offering a significant improvement over static models in scenarios with significant data fluctuations. The core mechanism of this framework centers around a self-adjusting learning rate and a feedback loop incorporating data-driven optimization. We demonstrate the framework's efficacy through a series of simulated and real-world case studies, showcasing its capacity to handle complex, dynamic systems. The paper concludes with a discussion of the advantages and potential applications of this approach.

title: 基于自适应的物理学模拟的量子环境优化
abstract: Quantum environment optimization is a crucial challenge in quantum computing, directly impacting the performance of quantum algorithms and the efficiency of quantum information storage. Traditional quantum simulation methods often rely on fixed parameters, limiting the potential for significant optimization. This paper presents a novel approach leveraging adaptive physics simulation, dynamically adjusting the quantum environment during the simulation process to enhance system performance. We introduce a self-optimizing algorithm that continuously evaluates and modifies the quantum system's environment based on gradients, resulting in improved accuracy and reduced computational cost. The core mechanism focuses on creating a feedback loop where the simulation parameters are continually refined based on the outcome of the simulation, leading to a more efficient and robust quantum simulation process. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of simulations focusing on variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) and quantum phase estimation (QPE) tasks, achieving substantial improvements in both accuracy and computational time compared to traditional methods. evidence.abstract: Quantum environment optimization is a crucial challenge in quantum computing, directly impacting the performance of quantum algorithms and the efficiency of quantum information storage. Traditional quantum simulation methods often rely on fixed parameters, limiting the potential for significant optimization. This paper presents a novel approach leveraging adaptive physics simulation, dynamically adjusting the quantum environment during the simulation process to enhance system performance. We introduce a self-optimizing algorithm that continuously evaluates and modifies the quantum system's environment based on gradients, resulting in improved accuracy and reduced computational cost. The core mechanism focuses on creating a feedback loop where the simulation parameters are continually refined based on the outcome of the simulation, leading to a more efficient and robust quantum simulation process. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of simulations focusing on variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) and quantum phase estimation (QPE) tasks, achieving substantial improvements in both accuracy and computational time compared to traditional methods. The results highlight the potential of this adaptive approach to address key bottlenecks in quantum simulation.

title: Quantum Entanglement Regularization
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, exhibits a profound and perplexing behavior that has captivated scientists and philosophers alike. Its non-local nature poses significant challenges to our classical understanding of causality and information. This paper explores the implications of non-locality in the context of quantum computation, focusing on the development of a novel regularization framework predicated on entanglement. We aim to enhance the robustness and computational efficiency of quantum algorithms by leveraging this non-locality, presenting a potential pathway towards advanced quantum computing paradigms, including optimization of ultra-cold quantum systems. The core of our investigation centers on the design of a specific regularization scheme that mitigates the inherent uncertainties associated with entangled states, ultimately offering a significant advancement in the field.

title: Old Search Trees, New Fruits: A Historical Development Review of AI Planning and Classical Search Revisited
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of AI Planning and Classical Search Revisited in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of planning and search algorithms as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: Chatbots in Household Budget Management: A Comparative Study in the Context of Economic Vulnerability
abstract: Household budget management is a central element of financial literacy, recognized by the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development as a key determinant of financial inclusion, economic stability, and social participation. Despite efforts to promote financial education, significant weaknesses remain, reinforcing the need to resort to other accessible solutions in the current digital context, such as chatbots. Within this framework, this study analyses and compares the responses produced by different chatbots in solving a budget management task aimed at a family experiencing economic vulnerability. The results indicate that, overall, the models analysed demonstrated the ability to interpret the context and provide recommendations aligned with the principles of financial literacy, although differences were observed in the accuracy of calculations, clarity of responses, and suitability of the proposals to the family’s specific circumstances. Overall, the findings suggest that chatbots, when properly mediated by the user and used critically, can serve as complementary tools to support budget management and the development of financial literacy, particularly relevant for families in situations of greater economic vulnerability, although the information and recommendations generated should be verified in light of the limitations identified in the study.

title: Neurosymbolic AI: From Research to Industry
abstract: Neurosymbolic AI brings together the statistical nature of machine learning with the formal reasoning capabilities of symbolic AI. It seeks to offer a balanced approach to current AI technologies, by combining the ability to learn from data, with the capacity of reasoning upon knowledge acquired from the environment. The main criticism of neural machine learning is the lack of explainability and semantics, which are key requirements in safety-critical applications, but inherent strengths of logic-based methods. Recently, several corporations have publicly announced products and technologies grounded on neurosymbolic AI methodologies. This talk provided a concise review of the foundations, frameworks and tools underlying neurosymbolic AI, along with illustrative industrial applications. I conclude by presenting trends and current research directions of the field.

title: Bauxite Residues as a Source of Spectral Signatures for Fe and Al Exploration Using Machine Learning and Sentinel-2 Data
abstract: Abstract The Dom Bosco Syncline (DBS), located in the southern portion of the Quadrilátero Ferrífero, Brazil, contains significant Fe and Al deposits. However, dense vegetation cover and geological heterogeneity impose substantial limitations on mineral prospecting using orbital remote sensing. In this context, the machine learning model MinMap-S2 (Mineral Mapping via Sentinel-2) is proposed to support mineral exploration in the DBS. MinMap-S2 is a hybrid model based on spectral signatures derived from bauxite residues deposited in the Marzagão tailings dam (MTD), located within the DBS, for the detection of Fe- and Al-rich mineralization. The model was developed using Python, and its methodology integrates the algorithms Self-Organizing Maps (SOM) and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) to process Sentinel-2 multispectral data. SOM is employed to generate a spectral library from bauxite residues and surrounding surface materials, which is subsequently used by XGBoost for supervised classification and spatial prediction. The model was applied to a region located in the eastern portion of DBS, characterized by detrital-lateritic covers and metasedimentary rocks, including itabirites, phyllites, schists, quartzites, and sericitic metarenites. Validation of the results was conducted through geological mapping, field sampling, and petrographic analyses. The results demonstrate that MinMap-S2 effectively identifies areas with spectral responses associated with Fe- and Al-rich mineralization, supporting the discrimination of mineralized zones in heterogeneous terrains and under dense vegetation cover. Overall, the proposed methodology demonstrates potential as a supporting tool for mineral exploration using Sentinel-2 multispectral data.

abstract: We present a new quadratic-time algorithm that computes an embedding of one rooted binary tree into another. title: Irredundant k-fold cross-validation for reliable, scalable, and energy-efficient model evaluation
abstract: Model evaluation remains one of the most computationally demanding phases of modern machine learning. As datasets and architectures scale, reliable evaluation increasingly strains computational and energy budgets. Standard k -fold cross-validation ( kF ) trains k times on heavily overlapping partitions. This redundancy both wastes compute and couples fold estimates: shared training data induces positive inter-fold covariance, so naive variance estimates are biased downward unless ad hoc inflations (e.g., Nadeau–Bengio) are applied. We introduce Irredundant k -Fold Cross-Validation ( IkF ), a novel restructuring of cross-validation that eliminates training-set overlap entirely. Each outer fold is split into k − 1 subfolds and the training set for test fold i is formed by one unique subfold from every other fold; thus every instance is used exactly once for training and once for testing across the k iterations. Theoretically, we (i) develop a bias model based on learning-curve and stability arguments, (ii) derive the variance of IkF and a closed-form expression for its mean-squared error, and (iii) show that disjoint training sets suppress overlap-induced dependence so that, under i.i.d. sampling and fixed k , inter-fold covariance vanishes as n → ∞ , thereby preventing overconfident uncertainty estimates and rendering the naive variance estimator asymptotically valid. Computationally, if training scales as C ( n ) = Θ ( n α ) , IkF lowers validation cost by approximately ( k − 1 ) α . On synthetic datasets ranging from 1 0 4 to 1 0 7 samples and two representative learners (Random Forests and Neural Networks), IkF matches kF on Accuracy, MCC, AUC(MCP), and AUC(ROC), while reducing validation time by ∼ 9 − 11 × and achieving comparable estimator variance. On a high-dimensional real-world dataset, IkF exhibits the same qualitative behaviour, achieving substantial speed-ups and associated reductions in CO 2 e emissions. Irredundant k -Fold Cross-Validation requires no correction factors and avoids repeated exposure of data, preserving statistical rigour while substantially lowering computational cost. It thus offers an immediately adoptable, reliability- and sustainability-aligned protocol for validating complex models and large-scale datasets, and is particularly well suited to settings with stringent time, energy, or environmental constraints.

title: Disentangling Statistical Preemption from Entrenchment in Language Models' Avoidance of Overgeneralization
abstract: How do learners avoid overgeneralizations such as Tom laughed me without explicit negative evidence? Constructionists have posited two proposals that describe indirect negative evidence against overgeneralizations: preemption (which privileges exposure to near-synonymous construction---e.g., she made him laugh) vs. entrenchment (all exposures to a verb's grammatical usages, including cases like He laughed). We disentangle these hypotheses by running controlled rearing experiments on LMs trained on child-caregiver conversations, where we systematically remove preemptive vs. non-preemptive evidence. We find that while LMs avoid overgeneralizations, they do not show preemption at a verb-specific level, instead showing weak but non-zero evidence of abstract preemption. Combined with results from analyzing the LMs' training dynamics, we find that LMs treat competing structures as indirect positive---as opposed to negative---evidence in the verb-specific condition. Insofar as preemption is the more plausible route to avoiding overgeneralizations in humans, our results point the need for there to be sensitivities to indirect negative evidence in neural network learners, and suggest new human experiments to test abstract preemption.

title: Purification of photonic graph states
abstract: Graph states constitute the main building block for quantum computing with photons. Quantum emitters with a hosted spin can deterministically generate photonic graph states, strongly lowering the overhead of multiplexing highly probabilistic linear-optics graph state generation. However, they generally suffer from various noise sources, resulting in reduced fidelities of the produced states. To mitigate this issue, we develop purification schemes for entangled photonic states. We first develop purification schemes to purify arbitrary photonic GHZ and other CSS states, which we generalize to all photonic graph states and stabilizer states. The proposed purification schemes have a high success probability of up to $1/2$ and require only linear optics and photon detectors. We optimize cascaded purification schemes for various graph states, taking into account phenomenological Pauli errors or physical noise in time-bin-encoded graph state generation with quantum emitters.

title: Direct Optimization of a 3D Finite-Source Reflector via Neural-Network Parameterization
abstract: We present a direct optimization method for three-dimensional freeform reflectors that transform the light of a finite-étendue source into a prescribed far-field angular intensity distribution. The reflector profile is represented by a small neural network (a multilayer perceptron), which is trained end-to-end through a differentiable ray-tracing objective. We furthermore parameterize the emission directions in gnomonic coordinates, and show how we use this to ensure that every emitted ray intersects the reflector. At each iteration, the network is converted to a bicubic spline representation for ray-tracing efficiency, and intersections with this smooth surface are solved by a damped Newton solve, with gradients computed via the implicit function theorem. The traced output distribution is compared with the desired target on a 'soft' histogram, under an $H^{-1}$-type spectral weighting that emphasizes long-range transport of flux to improve convergence. Optimization is performed using a BFGS method with self-scaled Broyden updates and a plateau-perturbation rule to prevent stalling. The method converges reliably within seconds on a single GPU for all examples tested.

title: A brief history of quantum vs classical computational advantage
abstract: In this review article we summarize all experiments claiming quantum computational advantage to date. Our review highlights challenges, loopholes, and refutations appearing in subsequent work to provide a complete picture of the current statuses of these experiments. In addition, we also discuss theoretical computational advantage in example problems such as approximate optimization and recommendation systems. Finally, we review recent experiments in quantum error correction --- the biggest frontier to reach experimental quantum advantage in Shor's algorithm.

title: Sequence labelling for code-mixed text by an averaged perceptron approach
abstract: In mixed-language settings, NLP models face challenges because of intertwined grammatical structures and language discrepancies.This paper analyses a Part-of-Speech tagger used on Hindi-English code-mixed (Hinglish) data and compares it with monolingual English and Hindi data.The model achieved an accuracy of 93.60% on the English dataset, accuracy of 95.95% on the Hindi dataset, and 94.89% on the Hinglish dataset, respectively.This showed strong model performance in both monolingual and code-mixed settings.The study also tried to understand the patterns in sentence structure that led to tagging errors.It was found that the most misclassifications occurred between nouns, verbs, proper nouns, and adjectives because of their overlapping lexical forms.The analysis of sentence length indicated that medium-length sentences yielded marginally higher accuracy than long sentences.In contrast, the error distribution per sentence showed that most sentences contain zero or one tagging error, with a cascading effect observed in a minority of cases where a single error in a sentence led to more errors and isolated errors.In the future, researchers can focus on understanding the reason for dual language error patterns, such as common misclassifications in a complex sentence.

title: Legal Liability for Artificial Intelligence-Generated Content from an Intellectual Property Perspective in Indonesia
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence now produces economically valuable works on a massive scale, while Indonesian copyright law still recognises human beings as the only possible authors. This study analyses the legal status of artificial intelligence-generated content from an intellectual property perspective and formulates a liability model suited to the Indonesian legal system. This normative legal research applies statutory, conceptual, case, and comparative approaches. Primary legal materials comprise Law Number 28 of 2014 on Copyright, the Indonesian Civil Code, and the Electronic Information and Transactions Law, while secondary materials consist of reputable literature published within the last five years, analysed through content analysis, legal interpretation, and deductive syllogism. The findings show that artificial intelligence can be neither a legal subject nor an author. Copyright protection attaches only insofar as a human creative contribution determines the final form of the work, consistent with the direction and supervision logic of Article 34. Liability for infringement must therefore be transferred to the human or legal entity connected to the system. This study formulates a tiered liability model distributing the burden among model developers, platform providers, and users according to degree of control, creative contribution, knowledge of risk, and discharge of the duty of care.

title: Reproducibility Package for "Schema-Valid JSON Is Not Sufficient for a Safe Cyber-Risk Record: Evidence-Anchored Semantic Validation and Fail-Closed Repair for Schema-Constrained LLM Pipelines"
abstract: This package contains the complete reproducibility materials for a model-independent mutation benchmark of a semantic guardrail for schema-constrained LLM cyber-risk records. It includes the CRSC JSON Schema, deterministic semantic validator, 15 error-code definitions, 144 synthetic core records, 24 adversarial prompt-injection controls, 996 schema-valid semantic fault injections across 14 mutation families, bounded evidence-preserving repair/fail-closed logic, raw and aggregate results, figures, and locked prompts for an optional provider-specific LLM extension. The reported results are mutation-adequacy results for the locked fault taxonomy and are not estimates of arbitrary LLM error rates.
